experiments.title: Torsion in cokernels: free abelian groups are not abelian
experiments.summary: Computes invariant factors (via gcds of minors) of all 625 integer 2 x 2 matrices with entries in -2..2. Whenever an invariant factor exceeds 1 the cokernel in Ab has torsion, and in free abelian groups the canonical coimage -> image map is not an isomorphism. Exact and exhaustive over that finite range.

experiments.title: The snake lemma, computed over a finite field
experiments.summary: Builds 300 seeded random morphisms of short exact sequences of F_5-vector spaces, computes kernels, cokernels and the connecting map by exact row reduction, and checks exactness of the six-term snake sequence at every term. Evidence for these cases only; the lesson proves the lemma in every abelian category.

experiments.title: Every action in a tiny world: which can be undone?
experiments.summary: Lists all n^n actions on a world of n things (n = 1 to 4), searches every candidate undo for each, and confirms that an action can be undone exactly when no two things end up the same; counts the actions undone by repeating them. Exhaustive for these tiny worlds only; the lesson proves one direction of the rule for every world.

experiments.title: Addition facts, take-away and place value, case by case
experiments.summary: Checks the turn-around rule and 'taking away undoes adding' on all 121 facts up to 10 + 10, shows that subtraction does not turn around, checks that every number below 100 has one tens-and-ones form and that comparing tens then ones orders all 10,000 pairs correctly, and runs the column methods with regrouping on every sum and difference up to 99. Exhaustive in this range only; the lesson gives the reasons.

experiments.title: Roth numbers, prime progressions and the sum-product phenomenon
experiments.summary: Computes the Roth numbers r3(N) for N <= 40 exactly by exhaustive backtracking, compares them with base-3 digit sets, finds the k-term progressions of primes with the smallest last term for k <= 7, and measures |A + A| and |A . A| for arithmetic and geometric progressions. Exact finite computations: they illustrate, but cannot test, asymptotic theorems such as Roth's and Green-Tao's.

experiments.title: Turan graphs and Ramsey numbers by exhaustive search
experiments.summary: Checks all 32768 labelled graphs on 6 vertices to confirm Turan's theorem there (ex(6, K3) = 9, ex(6, K4) = 12, extremal graphs exactly the Turan graphs), verifies that the Paley graph on 17 vertices has no 4-clique or independent 4-set, so R(4, 4) > 17, and tabulates probabilistic and Erdos-Szekeres bounds for R(k, k). Exhaustive for the cases shown only.

experiments.title: Galois connections from a relation: closed sets on both sides
experiments.summary: For the relation 'number n in 1..8 has property p' (even, odd, prime, square, divides 12, greater than 4), checks the Galois connection S <= down(T) iff T <= up(S) for all 256 x 64 pairs of subsets, and lists the closed sets on each side, which correspond bijectively. Exhaustive for this relation only.

experiments.title: Galois connections on finite lattices and currying, exhaustively
experiments.summary: Enumerates every monotone map between small lattices (a chain, the Boolean square, the divisors of 12) and checks that a right adjoint exists exactly for the maps preserving finite joins, computing it as u(b) = max{a : l(a) <= b}. Then verifies that currying is a natural bijection on small finite sets. Exhaustive for these examples only.

experiments.title: Jordan forms from ranks, and Cayley-Hamilton, exactly
experiments.summary: Computes the ranks of (A - lambda I)^k for an integer 5 x 5 matrix, reads off its Jordan blocks with the rank formula, checks the answer against SymPy's jordan_form, verifies chi_A(A) = 0 and the minimal polynomial in exact arithmetic, and exhibits two non-similar 4 x 4 matrices with the same characteristic and minimal polynomials. Exact checks for these matrices only.

experiments.title: Spectral theorem in floating point; the fragility of Jordan
experiments.summary: Diagonalises a seeded random symmetric matrix with orthonormal eigenvectors, checks the Rayleigh-quotient characterisation of the top eigenvalue by random sampling, measures the angle between eigenvectors of a non-normal matrix, and contrasts the stability of symmetric eigenvalues (Weyl) with the eps^(1/n) sensitivity of a Jordan block. Floating-point evidence, not proof.

experiments.title: Bezout's theorem by resultants
experiments.summary: For ten pairs of projective plane curves (lines, circles, a parabola, cuspidal and nodal cubics, an elliptic curve) computes the resultant after a generic change of coordinates, factors it over Q and reads off how many intersection points there are and with which multiplicities; the total is always d*e. Exact symbolic computation for these examples; the lesson explains and partly proves Bezout's theorem.

experiments.title: Points of curves over finite fields
experiments.summary: Counts the points of the projective plane, a conic, the cuspidal cubic and the elliptic curve y^2 = x^3 - x over F_p for all primes 3 <= p < 60, by brute force over P^2(F_p). Confirms p^2 + p + 1, p + 1, p + 1, Hasse's bound |a_p| <= 2 sqrt(p), a_p = 0 for p = 3 mod 4 and p = (a_p/2)^2 + b^2 for p = 1 mod 4 in that range; exhaustive for these primes only.

experiments.title: Class numbers by reduced forms and fundamental units
experiments.summary: Computes the class number of every imaginary quadratic field with fundamental discriminant -200 <= D < 0 by counting Gauss's reduced forms, checks each against Dirichlet's class number formula, lists the D with class number 1, and finds fundamental units of Z[sqrt d] from continued fractions. Exact and exhaustive in that range.

experiments.title: Splitting of primes in quadratic fields
experiments.summary: Factors every prime p < 200 in Q(i), Q(sqrt -5), Q(sqrt 2) and Q(sqrt 5) by counting roots of the minimal polynomial of the ring generator mod p (Dedekind-Kummer), checks agreement with the Kronecker symbol of the discriminant, and finds which split primes of Q(sqrt -5) have principal factors (p = a^2 + 5b^2). Exhaustive for p < 200 only.

experiments.title: A census of binary operations and of Z/nZ
experiments.summary: Checks all 19,683 operation tables on a 3-element set: counts the associative ones (113), the monoids and the groups, and confirms that no table has two identities and no monoid element has two inverses. Then finds for which n up to 40 every non-zero class of Z/nZ has an inverse (exactly the primes). Exhaustive for these cases only.

experiments.title: Homology of the sphere, torus, Klein bottle and projective plane
experiments.summary: Builds simplicial boundary matrices for explicit triangulations of S^2, the torus, the Klein bottle and RP^2, computes their Smith normal forms over Z and ranks over Z/2, and reports Betti numbers, torsion and the Euler characteristic. Exact for these complexes; independence of the triangulation is a theorem, not a consequence of the computation.

experiments.title: Lefschetz numbers and fixed points of maps of the torus
experiments.summary: For linear maps x -> Ax of the torus R^2/Z^2 it computes the Lefschetz number det(I - A) from the action on homology and counts fixed points exactly with rational arithmetic, confirming |L| = number of fixed points when L is nonzero. Exact for the listed matrices; it illustrates the Lefschetz theorem, it does not prove it.

experiments.title: Greedy algorithms: Kruskal, Dijkstra and making change
experiments.summary: Checks Kruskal's algorithm against exhaustive search over all spanning trees of 300 random graphs, Dijkstra against Bellman-Ford with and without negative edge weights (finding counterexamples in the second case), and greedy change-making against dynamic programming for all coin systems {1, a, b} with b <= 12.

experiments.title: Longest common subsequence: table, traceback and savings
experiments.summary: Fills the dynamic-programming table for the longest common subsequence of ABCBDAB and BDCABA, recovers an optimal subsequence by traceback, and counts how many calls the plain recursion makes on seeded random DNA strings compared with the (m+1)(n+1) cells of the table.

experiments.title: Comparisons in mergesort, insertion sort and the lower bound
experiments.summary: Counts the comparisons made by mergesort and insertion sort. For n <= 7 it tries all n! inputs, so the worst cases are exact and can be compared with the lower bound ceil(log2 n!) and the recurrence for mergesort; for n up to 1024 it averages over seeded random inputs and compares with n log2 n and n^2/4.

experiments.title: Linear and binary search: counting the comparisons
experiments.summary: Runs binary search for every target in sorted lists of every size n = 1..200 and finds the worst case is exactly floor(log2 n) + 1 probes; then counts probes for lists of up to 10^12 entries, against n comparisons for linear search. Exhaustive for n <= 200; the general bound is proved in the lesson.

experiments.title: Counting comparisons in insertion sort and merge sort
experiments.summary: Counts comparisons made by insertion sort and merge sort on all orderings of up to 7 items (exact worst cases) and on seeded random lists of 100 and 1000 numbers, beside the lower bound log2(n!) for any comparison sort. Exhaustive for n <= 7; the random runs are one seeded sample each, not averages over all inputs.

experiments.title: Counting primes up to a million
experiments.summary: Sieves the primes below 10^6 and tabulates pi(x), x/log x and li(x) at powers of 10, the ratio pi(x)/(x/log x) and the growing difference, Chebyshev's psi(x)/x, and the race between primes 1 and 3 mod 4 with its first lead change at 26861. Exact counts and numerical approximations at finitely many points; no limit is proved.

experiments.title: Zeros of zeta and the explicit formula
experiments.summary: Evaluates zeta(s) by Euler-Maclaurin summation, finds the first ten zeros on the critical line as sign changes of Hardy's Z-function, compares them with published values and with the Riemann-von Mangoldt count, and rebuilds psi(x) from those zeros with von Mangoldt's explicit formula. Numerical evidence; says nothing about zeros off the line.

experiments.title: Same perimeter, different area: rectangles and pentominoes
experiments.summary: Lists every whole-number rectangle with perimeter 24 (areas from 11 to 36, largest for the 6 x 6 square) and every rectangle with area 24 (perimeters from 20 to 50). Then builds all 63 shapes of five unit squares (up to sliding) and counts their perimeters exactly. Exhaustive for these cases only.

experiments.title: Measuring the angles of many triangles
experiments.summary: Measures the angles of 1000 random grid triangles and 300 random convex quadrilaterals from their coordinates. The sums are 180 and 360 degrees up to rounding errors of about 1e-12 degrees. Also shows that longer arms do not change an angle. Numerical evidence for these shapes only; the proof is in the lesson.

experiments.title: The chord-and-tangent group law in exact arithmetic
experiments.summary: Implements the group law on y^2 = x^3 + ax + b with exact fractions. Shows that (2, 3) has order 6 on y^2 = x^3 + 1, that (3, 5) on y^2 = x^3 - 2 has multiples with rapidly growing denominators (quadratic growth of height), and checks associativity on all triples of points of a curve over F_13: exact, exhaustive for that one curve only.

experiments.title: Point counts mod p: Hasse, Sato-Tate and Birch-Swinnerton-Dyer
experiments.summary: Counts points of four elliptic curves over F_p for all primes p < 1000 (exact). Checks the Hasse bound in every case, tabulates the Sato-Tate angles of 37a1 against the predicted density, and recomputes the Euler products that led Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer to their conjecture. The last two parts are numerical illustrations, not evidence strong enough to prove or even test the asymptotic statements.

experiments.title: Finite shadows of Zorn's lemma, and a well-order of Q
experiments.summary: Runs the Zorn-style 'climb until maximal' argument where it needs no choice: extends independent sets in (Z/2)^4 to bases (all 840 counted), finds the maximal ideals of Z/n for n <= 60 by searching the poset of ideals (always the primes dividing n), and well-orders the positive rationals explicitly by the Calkin-Wilf sequence. Exact and exhaustive for these finite cases; infinite posets are where Zorn is needed.

experiments.title: The cumulative hierarchy V_0, ..., V_5 in Ackermann's coding
experiments.summary: Codes hereditarily finite sets by natural numbers (y is in x iff bit y of x is 1), builds V_0, ..., V_5, computes ranks by recursion, and checks exhaustively that V_k is the set of codes below |V_k| = 2^|V_(k-1)|, that x is in V_k iff rank(x) < k, and that foundation and transitivity hold. Finite stages only: nothing here reaches V_omega or beyond.

experiments.title: Cantor's diagonal trick on a finite list
experiments.summary: Builds the diagonal-flipped sequence for a fixed list of 8 infinite binary sequences and checks exactly that it differs from every listed sequence. The finite run illustrates the mechanism only; the proof that the infinite binary sequences cannot be listed is Cantor's general argument.

experiments.title: Ordinal arithmetic in Cantor normal form
experiments.summary: Implements ordinals below epsilon_0 in Cantor normal form with exact comparison, addition and multiplication. Shows 1 + w = w < w + 1 and 2w = w < w2, tests associativity and both distributive laws on 3000 random triples (right distributivity fails), and follows Goodstein sequences alongside their strictly decreasing ordinals. The random tests are evidence; the laws are proved by transfinite induction.

experiments.title: Schroeder-Bernstein bijections by chain-chasing
experiments.summary: Builds the Schroeder-Bernstein bijection h from two injections by classifying backward chains (stopping in A, stopping in B, or endless), for [0, 1] vs [0, 1) with f(x) = x/2 and g(y) = y on exact rational points, and for N vs Z. Checks injectivity and that every target in a finite window is hit. Exact, but only for finitely many points: bijectivity on the whole sets is the theorem.

experiments.title: λ-terms in finite sets: Church numerals and naturality
experiments.summary: Computes the meaning of Church numerals over finite base sets and finds the first two distinct numerals with the same meaning (so finite models are not complete for beta-eta equality), then checks by exhaustive search that exactly four of the 256 functions X*X -> X*X on a two-element set are natural, matching the four closed normal terms of that type.

experiments.title: Heyting algebras of open sets on small spaces
experiments.summary: Enumerates all topologies on a set with at most three points, checks the Heyting residuation law exhaustively, counts the Boolean ones (exactly the partition topologies) and evaluates classical tautologies under every valuation. Failures are genuine countermodels to intuitionistic derivability; successes are evidence on finitely many algebras only.

experiments.title: Fusion rings from groups, and the Fibonacci ring
experiments.summary: Builds S3, D4 and Q8 as matrix groups, finds all one-dimensional characters by brute force, adds the trace of a 2-dimensional representation, checks orthonormality and computes the fusion rings exactly: D4 and Q8 are non-isomorphic groups with isomorphic fusion rings. Then approximates the Frobenius-Perron dimensions of the Fibonacci and Ising rings (golden ratio, sqrt 2) by power iteration.

experiments.title: Khovanov homology of the trefoil and figure-eight knots
experiments.summary: Builds Khovanov's cube of smoothings from a PD code, with the Frobenius algebra Q[x]/(x^2) on circles, checks d o d = 0, and computes the graded Euler characteristic (the unnormalised Jones polynomial) and the rational Khovanov homology of the left-handed trefoil and the figure-eight knot. Exact for these diagrams; invariance is Khovanov's theorem.

experiments.title: Monos and epis in finite sets, by brute force
experiments.summary: Enumerates every function between sets of size 0 to 3, decides whether it is a monomorphism or an epimorphism straight from the cancellation definitions (testing against every map from or to a set of size at most 2), and checks that monos are exactly the injections and epis exactly the surjections. Exhaustive for these sizes only; the proof in the lesson covers all sets.

experiments.title: Does the order of two actions matter?
experiments.summary: Checks every pair of six number actions on the starting numbers 0 to 20, and every pair of four moves of an L-shaped tile, to see whether doing them in either order gives the same result. Two additions, two multiplications, two turns or two flips can be swapped; an addition and a multiplication, or a quarter turn and a flip, cannot.

experiments.title: Undoing a chain: reverse order or same order?
experiments.summary: Builds all 36 two-step and 216 three-step chains from six undoable actions, runs each on the starting numbers 0 to 10 with exact fractions, and undoes it either in reverse order or in the same order. Reverse order always returns to the start (the socks-and-shoes rule); the same order works only for some chains.

experiments.title: Chaining tables, and undoing chains in the right order
experiments.summary: Chains functions stored as tables (people -> cities -> continents). For all 27 functions on {0, 1, 2} it checks the identity laws, finds the 6 that can be undone, confirms the socks-and-shoes rule on all 36 pairs of them, and finds that undoing in the wrong order works exactly for the 18 pairs that commute. It also converts 30 C to F and back with exact fractions. Exhaustive for this 3-element set only.

experiments.title: Every typo of 300 code numbers, caught or missed
experiments.summary: Builds 300 valid ISBN-10, ISBN-13, Luhn and digit-sum codes from seeded random digits, applies every single-digit error, neighbour swap and jump swap, and counts how many damaged codes each scheme rejects: ISBN-10 catches all three kinds, ISBN-13 misses neighbour swaps of digits five apart, Luhn misses 09/90, and the digit sum misses every swap.

experiments.title: A parity bit on a noisy line
experiments.summary: Sends 10,000 eight-bit words (7 data bits and a parity bit) through a simulated channel that flips each bit with probability p, for three values of p, and counts intact, rejected and undetected-damaged words. The counts are compared with exact binomial probabilities. Simulation is statistical evidence; the formulas follow from the parity theorem.

experiments.title: Kepler orbits: Verlet versus Euler
experiments.summary: Integrates the inverse-square law for an elliptic orbit with the velocity Verlet method and with explicit Euler, measures energy and angular momentum drift, the period, perihelion and aphelion, and compares them with Kepler's laws (e = 0.44, T = 2 pi a^1.5). Numerical evidence for one orbit; the conservation laws and Kepler's laws are proved in the lesson.

experiments.title: Pendulum period: small angles, elliptic integrals, simulation
experiments.summary: Computes the exact period of a pendulum for several amplitudes with Gauss's arithmetic-geometric mean (elliptic integral), compares it with the small-angle period, a two-term series correction and a velocity Verlet simulation. Shows that the period grows with amplitude and diverges as the amplitude approaches 180 degrees.

experiments.title: Clock arithmetic: which residues have inverses?
experiments.summary: Prints the addition and multiplication tables mod 6, finds by search which residues have multiplicative inverses mod 6 and mod 7, and checks for every k from 2 to 30 that these are exactly the a with gcd(a, k) = 1. The table proves the pattern only for k <= 30; for every k it is a theorem (from Bezout's identity) proved elsewhere.

experiments.title: Sorting and counting a market basket
experiments.summary: Sorts a fixed basket of market items by kind and by colour and counts each group exactly, then checks every one of the 720 orders of a 6-item basket gives the same counts. This proves order-independence for that basket only; why it holds for every finite collection is explained in the lesson, not by this program.

experiments.title: Inclusion-exclusion, derangements and birthdays
experiments.summary: Counts the numbers up to N divisible by 2, 3 or 5 directly and by inclusion-exclusion; counts derangements of n hats by listing all n! arrangements (n <= 8) and by the inclusion-exclusion formula, watching the fraction approach 1/e; and computes the exact birthday probabilities, which pass 1/2 at 23 people but reach 1 only at 366, where the pigeonhole principle applies.

experiments.title: Pascal's triangle three ways, and the binomial theorem
experiments.summary: Counts k-element subsets by listing them (n <= 12), by Pascal's rule and by the factorial formula (n <= 40), and checks symmetry, row sums 2^n and alternating row sums 0 on the same range; SymPy confirms that the coefficients of (x + y)^n are the rows of the triangle for n <= 12. Exhaustive over a finite range only: the lesson's proofs cover every n.

experiments.title: Radicals and the Nullstellensatz by Groebner bases
experiments.summary: Uses Groebner bases over Q to decide ideal membership, finds the least k with f^k in I for tangent intersections (parabola and line, circle and tangent line, a cusp), and checks that this agrees with Rabinowitsch's single test 1 in (I, 1 - t f). It also shows an ideal with no real zeros that is proper because it has complex zeros. Exact checks of examples; the Nullstellensatz is proved in the lesson.

experiments.title: Spec, localisation and Nakayama in the rings Z/n
experiments.summary: For every n <= 60 lists the ideals of Z/n, finds the prime and maximal ideals, the nilradical and the Jacobson radical, decides whether Z/n is local, computes the localisation at each prime from the definition, and checks Nakayama's lemma for every ideal of every local Z/p^e in range. Exhaustive in that range; the lesson proves the general statements.

experiments.title: Do the paths agree? Testing squares of functions
experiments.summary: Tests whether squares of functions commute on -50..50 and prints the first disagreement; searches for counterexamples to f(a + b) = f(a) + f(b) for 100x, x + 1, x*x, -3x and the Celsius-to-Fahrenheit rule; checks all 3125 functions on {0..4} and finds exactly 5 that preserve addition mod 5 (multiplication by m); and checks all 16384 fillings of two squares on {0, 1} to confirm pasting and refute its converse.

experiments.title: Compactness via Koenig's lemma: colouring N level by level
experiments.summary: Builds the tree of proper colourings of {0, ..., n - 1} for 'distance graphs' on N (numbers joined when their difference is in D). For D = {1, 3, 4} and 3 colours the tree dies at level 7, a finite obstruction; for D = {2, 3, 5, 7} and 4 colours it has many dead ends but survives to level 24, and a surviving branch is the colouring by n mod 4. Exact up to level 24; Koenig's lemma supplies the infinite part.

experiments.title: Consistent iff satisfiable: resolution versus truth tables
experiments.summary: Saturates 150 random sets of 3-literal clauses over 4 variables under the resolution rule and compares 'no contradiction derivable' with 'some truth assignment satisfies every clause' (soundness and completeness of resolution). For consistent sets it builds a model Lindenbaum-style, one variable at a time, and checks it. Exact for each set; the sample is random, so this tests rather than proves the theorem.

experiments.title: Contour integrals by computer: Cauchy, residues, zeros
experiments.summary: Computes contour integrals around circles with the trapezoid rule (geometrically convergent for analytic periodic integrands): 1/z and conj(z) give 2 pi i, z^2 gives 0, Cauchy's formula recovers e^0.5, two real integrals match their residue values pi and pi/e, and the argument principle counts the zeros of z^5 - 3z + 1 in the unit disc. Numerical evidence only.

experiments.title: Hodge diamonds of hypersurfaces by counting monomials
experiments.summary: Counts monomials in the Jacobian ring of a Fermat hypersurface to get its middle Hodge numbers (Griffiths' theorem), builds the Hodge diamond of curves, the quartic K3 surface and the quintic threefold (h^{2,1} = 101), and checks the Euler characteristic against the Chern-class formula and the Hodge symmetries. Exact arithmetic; the theorems that give these numbers their meaning are cited, not proved.

experiments.title: The Kahler condition in coordinates: Fubini-Study versus Hopf
experiments.summary: Uses SymPy to test the Kahler condition d_k g_{i jbar} = d_i g_{k jbar} for three Hermitian metrics on C^2: flat, Fubini-Study (Kahler, with potential log(1 + |z|^2)) and the scale-invariant Hopf metric |dz|^2/|z|^2 (not Kahler). It also integrates the Fubini-Study area of CP^1, which is pi. Exact symbolic computation, trusted as far as SymPy's algebra is.

experiments.title: Roots of unity and De Moivre's theorem
experiments.summary: Computes the n-th roots of unity in floating point for n = 3..8 and checks z^n = 1, sum 0, product (-1)^(n+1) and side 2 sin(pi/n) up to rounding; uses SymPy for the exact cube roots of 1 and to derive cos 3t = 4cos^3 t - 3cos t from De Moivre; shows why sqrt(ab) = sqrt(a) sqrt(b) fails for negative a, b.

experiments.title: Complex multiplication and sums of two squares
experiments.summary: Checks N(zw) = N(z) N(w) for all Gaussian integers z, w with coordinates in -6..6 (exact integers, 28561 pairs), then multiplies Gaussian integers to build sums of two squares: 5 * 13 = 65 = 1 + 64 = 16 + 49. The grid is evidence; the identity is proved by algebra.

experiments.title: Karp's reduction from 3-SAT to independent set, tested
experiments.summary: Builds the 3-SAT to INDEPENDENT-SET graph for 200 seeded random 3-CNF formulas (some with a planted unsatisfiable core), decides satisfiability and the existence of an independent set of size m by separate exhaustive searches, and checks that they always agree. Experimental evidence for the reduction on small formulas, not a proof.

experiments.title: Random 3-SAT: the satisfiability threshold and the hard region
experiments.summary: Solves 30 seeded random 3-CNF formulas on 20 variables at each of eight clause densities with a DPLL solver, reporting the fraction satisfiable and the mean search effort. Every satisfiable verdict is re-checked with its certificate. Statistical evidence at one small size only; it does not establish the threshold or any complexity bound.

experiments.title: Composing functions: associative, but order matters
experiments.summary: Checks associativity of composition on all 19683 triples of functions on a 3-element set and the identity laws on all 27 functions (a proof for that set only), and finds functions with g o f != f o g, a counterexample showing composition is not commutative in general.

experiments.title: All two-state Turing machines: halting runs and non-halting proofs
experiments.summary: Enumerates all 20736 two-state, two-symbol Turing machines, runs each on a blank tape, and either watches it halt or finds a sound certificate that it never halts (unreachable halt, repeated configuration, translated cycle). Every machine is classified, which yields S(2) = 6 and Sigma(2) = 4, as far as this code is correct.

experiments.title: Simulating Turing machines: a binary counter and a unary adder
experiments.summary: Simulates a one-state binary incrementer on every input below 256 and a three-state unary adder on all pairs m, n <= 12, checking every output exactly and recording step counts. Exhaustive for those ranges only: it is evidence of correctness, not a proof for all inputs.

experiments.title: Summing the same numbers in different orders
experiments.summary: Shows that floating-point addition is not associative, then sums 100,000 seeded random numbers in several orders and by pairwise, Kahan and math.fsum summation. Errors are measured against the exact rational sum (computed with integers) and compared with the proven worst-case bound for recursive summation. The exact sums are exact; the float results are this machine's IEEE 754 arithmetic.

experiments.title: Seeds, fingerprints and confidence intervals in Monte Carlo
experiments.summary: Estimates the integral of exp(-x^2) on [0, 1] by Monte Carlo. With a fixed seed two runs agree bit for bit (checked by a 64-bit FNV-1a fingerprint); different seeds give different estimates, reported with standard errors. Over 200 seeds it counts how often the nominal 95% interval covers the exact value (via erf): statistical evidence about the method.

experiments.title: Inverses, linear congruences and the Chinese remainder theorem
experiments.summary: Uses the extended Euclidean algorithm to find inverses modulo n, to solve linear congruences ax = b (mod n) (gcd(a, n) solutions or none) and to solve systems by the Chinese remainder theorem, including Sunzi's problem. Checks exhaustively that Z/105Z -> Z/3 x Z/5 x Z/7 is a bijection and that non-coprime moduli can be inconsistent.

experiments.title: Fermat, Euler, Wilson and the Carmichael numbers
experiments.summary: Checks Fermat's little theorem for all primes below 200, Euler's theorem for all n below 200 and Wilson's theorem (both directions) below 400. Then finds every composite n < 10,000 that passes the Fermat test to base 2, and keeps those that pass for every coprime base: the seven Carmichael numbers below 10,000, counterexamples to the converse of Fermat.

experiments.title: Which curve is this second-degree equation?
experiments.summary: Classifies equations Ax^2 + Bxy + Cy^2 + Dx + Ey + F = 0 as ellipse, circle, parabola, hyperbola or a degenerate case (point, lines, empty) from exact integer invariants, for named examples and for all 15,500 equations with coefficients in -2..2 and a non-zero quadratic part. Exact computation of a standard classification, not a proof of it.

experiments.title: Ray tracing: the reflective properties of conics
experiments.summary: Traces 9 vertical rays into the parabola y = x^2/4 and 12 rays from one focus of the ellipse x^2/25 + y^2/9 = 1, reflecting each by the law of reflection, and measures how close the reflected rays come to the focus (parabola) or the other focus (ellipse). Numerical evidence for finitely many rays; the lesson proves the property for all rays.

experiments.title: Reflections and grid distances, point by point
experiments.summary: Checks on all 121 whole-number points from -5 to 5 (and some fraction points) that reflecting twice in an axis returns each point, that reflection in the x-axis swaps quadrants 1 and 4 and 2 and 3, which points it fixes, and that reflections, the half turn and swapping the coordinates keep grid distances between all 14,641 pairs of points.

experiments.title: Diagonal arguments on finite lists
experiments.summary: Checks all 512 functions from a 3-element set to its power set and finds the diagonal set missing from every image; builds the decimal diagonal (digits 4 and 5 only) for a list of ten numbers; and shows that a naive digit rule can output 0.4999... = 0.5, a number already on the list. Finite illustrations of the general proofs in the lesson.

experiments.title: Listing the integers, pairs and rationals
experiments.summary: Runs the zigzag listing of Z, Cantor's pairing function N x N -> N with its inverse (checked to be mutually inverse for every value below 100000), and the Calkin-Wilf listing of the positive rationals, checking that its first 2047 terms are all different and include every fraction p/q with p, q <= 10. Finite checks; the bijections are proved in the lesson.

experiments.title: Counting a herd of goats in every order
experiments.summary: Counts a herd of five goats in all 120 possible orders and records the last number word said each time (always 'five'), shows how skipping a goat or touching one twice changes the answer, and compares children with cups by pairing. Exhaustive for this herd only; why the count never depends on the order, for any collection, is explained in the lesson.

experiments.title: Counting functions, injections and surjections
experiments.summary: Lists every function between sets of sizes 1 to 4, counts the injective, surjective and bijective ones exactly, and compares the counts with n^m, the falling factorial and the inclusion-exclusion formula. Agreement for these sizes is proved by enumeration; that the formulas hold for all sizes is a theorem the enumeration does not establish.

experiments.title: Counting principles checked by listing every case
experiments.summary: Compares formula counts with brute-force enumeration: 4-digit PINs (10^4), PINs without repeats (10*9*8*7) and with a repeat (complement), podium finishes (8*7*6), arrangements of 5 letters (5!), 3-symbol codes with at least one digit (36^3 - 26^3), and numbers up to 100 divisible by 2 or 5 (50 + 20 - 10). Exhaustive for these cases; the principles themselves are proved in the lesson.

experiments.title: How fast factorials grow: exact values and Stirling's formula
experiments.summary: Prints exact factorials beside 2^n and 10^n, finds where n! overtakes them (n = 4 and n = 25), counts the 68 digits of 52!, estimates the time to list every shuffle of a deck, and compares n! with Stirling's approximation, whose relative error shrinks roughly like 1/(12n). Exact integers plus floating-point estimates; Stirling's formula is quoted, not proved.

experiments.title: Diffie-Hellman and the cost of discrete logarithms
experiments.summary: Runs a toy Diffie-Hellman exchange modulo a prime, then counts the group operations needed to recover a secret exponent by exhaustive search (about p) and by baby-step giant-step (about sqrt(p)) for primes from about 10^3 to 10^9. Exact counts for these cases; an illustration of growth, not a proof that the problem is hard.

experiments.title: Toy RSA: keys, fast powering and a broken small key
experiments.summary: Generates a seeded 36-bit toy RSA key with Miller-Rabin primes, encrypts and decrypts with repeated squaring (counting multiplications), shows that textbook RSA is deterministic and malleable, and breaks the key by trial division. Correctness is checked exactly on examples; nothing here measures the security of real RSA.

experiments.title: Theorema Egregium on examples, and Gauss-Bonnet for an ellipsoid
experiments.summary: Computes with SymPy the fundamental forms and Gaussian curvature of a sphere, catenoid, helicoid, saddle and cylinder, both from the shape in space and from E, F, G alone (Brioschi's formula), and checks that they agree. It shows the catenoid and helicoid share E, F, G and K, and integrates K dA over an ellipsoid numerically, getting 4 pi. Symbolic and numerical evidence on examples only.

experiments.title: Total curvature of closed curves: Hopf, Fenchel, Fary-Milnor
experiments.summary: Integrates the curvature of closed curves numerically. Plane curves (circle, ellipse, limacon, figure eight) give 2 pi times their turning numbers 1, 1, 2, 0; space curves give total curvature 2 pi for a convex plane curve and more than 4 pi for a trefoil knot, as the theorems of Fenchel and Fary-Milnor predict; a helix's curvature matches a/(a^2+b^2). Numerical evidence for these curves only.

experiments.title: A class survey: tallies, picture graphs and totals
experiments.summary: Tallies 24 survey answers into four categories, draws a tally chart and a picture graph, answers 'most' and 'how many more', shows how pictures of different sizes mislead and how multiple answers overcount, and checks all 4,096 ways six children can answer that the totals add up to six. Exact; the exhaustive check is for that small case only.

experiments.title: The mean as a fair share: levelling towers
experiments.summary: Levels towers of cubes by moving one cube at a time from a tallest to a shortest tower, printing every step, and checks that the final level equals total / number of towers (and that the mean need not be a data value). Then computes the exact mean of measurements in quarters with fractions. Exact for these data sets.

experiments.title: Misleading bar charts: when the axis does not start at zero
experiments.summary: Draws bars for 52 kg and 48 kg as text with the axis starting at 0 and at 40, and computes the apparent ratio of the bars for several starting values (from 13/12 up to 5). Then checks every whole-number case 0 < b < c < a <= 60 that a raised axis exaggerates the ratio. Exact; exhaustive only up to 60.

experiments.title: Ext from resolutions and from extensions
experiments.summary: Computes Ext^n(M, N) for finite cyclic modules over Z and over Z/N as cohomology of Hom(P, N) for explicit projective resolutions P, by counting kernels and images element by element; then counts extensions of Z/p by Z/p as symmetric 2-cocycles modulo coboundaries for p = 2, 3. Exact for these small cases, which illustrate Ext^n = Hom_D(M, N[n]).

experiments.title: Closed sets as trees: perfect versus countable
experiments.summary: Counts nodes and computes splitting heights of four pruned binary trees truncated at depths up to 16, and tests whether every node branches. A perfect tree and a countable 'staircase' tree turn out to have identical counts and splitting heights: the perfect set dichotomy is a theorem about infinite trees that finite truncations cannot decide.

experiments.title: Exterior calculus on R^3: wedge, d, and d d = 0
experiments.summary: Implements differential forms on R^3 as dictionaries of SymPy coefficients, with the wedge product and the exterior derivative. With arbitrary coefficient functions it verifies d(dw) = 0 in degrees 0 to 2, graded anticommutativity, the Leibniz rule, and that d is grad, curl and div; it then checks the divergence theorem exactly on the unit cube for one field. Symbolic verification on examples.

experiments.title: Line integrals: exact forms, the angle form and Green's theorem
experiments.summary: Integrates 1-forms along paths by pulling them back to [0, 1]. An exact form gives 0 around every loop; the closed angle form d theta gives 2 pi times the winding number, and +pi or -pi between the same endpoints along different half circles, so it is not exact; x dy - y dx gives twice the enclosed area, as Green's theorem predicts. Numerical evidence on sample paths.

experiments.title: Counting preimages with and without signs
experiments.summary: For a degree-3 map of the circle that folds back, finds all preimages of several regular values: their number varies (5 or 7) but the count with signs of the derivative is always 3; also lists the critical values. Then counts preimages for the holomorphic map z^3 - 3z (degree 3, critical values -2 and 2) and for conj(z)^3 (degree -3). Numerical evidence.

experiments.title: Indices of vector fields and the Poincare-Hopf theorem
experiments.summary: Computes indices of isolated zeros of planar vector fields by summing angle changes round small circles; checks that the indices of several fields on the sphere (written in two stereographic charts) add up to 2 and that the gradient of the height function on a torus has indices adding up to 0, as the Poincare-Hopf theorem predicts. Numerical.

experiments.title: Euclid's algorithm: steps, Bezout and Lame's bound
experiments.summary: Traces the extended Euclidean algorithm on 1071 and 462 (gcd 21 = 1071*(-3) + 462*7), then counts division steps for every pair a > b with b below 10, 100 and 1000 (a below 1000 in the last range), finding that consecutive Fibonacci numbers are slowest and that Lame's bound of five steps per digit holds there. Exhaustive in those ranges only.

experiments.title: Hilbert numbers and the chance of being coprime
experiments.summary: Finds every Hilbert number (4k + 1) up to 1500 with two different factorisations into Hilbert irreducibles (441 = 9*49 = 21*21 is the first), confirms unique prime factorisation for ordinary integers in the same range, and counts coprime pairs up to N = 100000, whose proportion approaches 6/pi^2 = 0.6079... Finite and numerical evidence only.

experiments.title: Logistic map: periods, Feigenbaum's delta and Lyapunov exponents
experiments.summary: Iterates x -> r x (1 - x): detects attractor periods for several r, computes the superstable parameters of the period-doubling cascade by Newton's method and shows the gap ratios approaching Feigenbaum's delta = 4.669, and estimates Lyapunov exponents (exactly ln 2 at r = 4). Floating-point evidence over finitely many iterates.

experiments.title: Sensitive dependence: true orbits versus floating point
experiments.summary: Uses the conjugacy x = sin^2(pi theta) between the logistic map at r = 4 and the doubling map, with exact fractions for theta, to compute true orbits and compare them with floating-point iteration: the simulation departs from the true orbit after about 50 steps, nearby true orbits separate like 2^n, and the float doubling map collapses to 0 although exact orbits of 1/7 are periodic.

experiments.title: Pell's equation by continued fractions
experiments.summary: Computes the periodic continued fraction of sqrt(d) with exact integer arithmetic, reads off the fundamental solution of x^2 - d y^2 = 1 for every non-square d up to 30 and for d = 61 and 109, verifies each solution exactly, and generates further solutions by composition. Exact for the d shown; that the method always works is proved in the lesson.

experiments.title: Primitive roots and Artin's conjecture
experiments.summary: Decides for every n up to 60 whether (Z/nZ)^x is cyclic and checks the classification n = 1, 2, 4, p^k, 2p^k; finds least primitive roots; and measures how often 2 is a primitive root modulo primes below 50000, compared with Artin's constant 0.3739558 (a conjectured density, proved only under the generalised Riemann hypothesis). Statistical for Artin.

experiments.title: Quadratic reciprocity and sums of two squares by computer
experiments.summary: Checks quadratic reciprocity, Gauss's lemma and Eisenstein's lattice-point count for all pairs of distinct odd primes below 200, verifies the supplementary laws for -1 and 2, and finds which primes below 100 are sums of two squares (exactly 2 and those = 1 mod 4). Exhaustive for these ranges; the proofs for all primes are in the lesson.

experiments.title: Truth values in presheaf toposes
experiments.summary: Computes the sieves Omega(p) for presheaves on small finite posets, checks exhaustively for all presheaves on {0 < 1} with at most 4 and 3 sections that the characteristic map is a bijection from subpresheaves to natural maps into Omega, and computes Heyting negation on truth values, exhibiting failures of excluded middle. Finite cases only: the general theorems are proved in the lesson.

experiments.title: Shortest paths as free Lawvere metric spaces
experiments.summary: Computes the shortest-path distance of a small directed graph of uphill/downhill walking times by min-plus matrix multiplication (free [0, inf]-enriched category), checks d(x, x) = 0, the triangle inequality and D (x) D = D on all triples, counts asymmetric pairs, computes reachability with (or, and), and checks the asymmetric Hausdorff distance on all sets of places.

experiments.title: Necklaces, bracelets and cubes: brute force versus Burnside
experiments.summary: Counts necklaces (rotations) and bracelets (rotations and reflections) with n <= 9 beads in 2 or 3 colours, and face colourings of a cube under its 24 rotations, both by brute-force orbit enumeration and by Burnside's lemma, and shows that the naive count k^n/n is wrong. Exhaustive for these sizes.

experiments.title: Exponential generating functions versus brute-force counting
experiments.summary: Expands the EGFs exp(e^x - 1), exp(x + x^2/2) and e^(-x)/(1 - x) with exact fractions and compares their coefficients with brute-force counts of set partitions, involutions and derangements for n <= 7, then checks |D(n)/n! - 1/e| <= 1/(n+1)! numerically. Exact for the sizes shown.

experiments.title: Partitions: generating functions, Euler's theorem, Glaisher's map
experiments.summary: Expands the generating functions for all partitions, odd-part partitions and distinct-part partitions exactly up to x^60, checks Euler's theorem there, runs Glaisher's bijection on all partitions of 8, compares p(n) with the Hardy-Ramanujan formula, and tests Ramanujan's congruence mod 5 for n < 300. Finite checks only.

experiments.title: A relation checker: counterexamples and classes
experiments.summary: Tests six relations on small finite sets - same remainder, differ by at most 1, divides, less than, same number of letters and share a letter - for reflexivity, symmetry and transitivity by checking every case. Prints a counterexample for each failure and the equivalence classes of each equivalence relation, checking that they form a partition. Valid for these finite sets only.

experiments.title: Equivalence relations and partitions, counted exhaustively
experiments.summary: Runs through every relation on a 3-element set (512) and every symmetric relation on sets of up to 4 elements, testing reflexivity, symmetry and transitivity. Checks that taking equivalence classes matches equivalence relations one-to-one with partitions (counted by the Bell numbers 1, 2, 5, 15) and counts the symmetric, transitive relations that fail to be reflexive. Exhaustive for n <= 4 only; the lesson's proof covers all sets.

experiments.title: Birkhoff averages: rotations, doubling and continued fractions
experiments.summary: Computes Birkhoff averages for an irrational and a rational rotation, the non-mixing overlaps of the golden rotation, the collapse of the doubling map in floating point versus exact arithmetic on random bits, and the frequencies of continued fraction digits of random numbers against the Gauss-Kuzmin law, plus a check of the invariance of the Gauss measure. Finite orbits and seeded random samples: evidence, not proof.

experiments.title: Rounding errors: the worst case and the typical case
experiments.summary: Checks all 216,000 lists of three numbers below 60: the rounded-first total is always within 5 x 3 = 15 of the exact total, and it differs from the rounded exact total in a known fraction of cases. Then simulates seeded random shopping lists and compares the worst-case error 5k with the typical error, which grows much more slowly. The simulation is statistical evidence only.

experiments.title: Rounding halves: up, to even, or down?
experiments.summary: Rounds every whole number from 0 to 9,999 to the nearest ten with three rules (halves up, halves to even, always down) and computes each rule's average error exactly: +0.5, 0 and -4.5. Shows that Python's round() rounds halves to even, and that round(2.675, 2) = 2.67 because the float stored for 2.675 is slightly smaller than 2.675.

experiments.title: Inscribed angles, measured
experiments.summary: Measures the angle APB for 2,000 seeded random points P on each arc of a chord AB of the unit circle and compares it with the inscribed angle theorem (half the central angle, or 180 degrees minus that), including Thales' case of a diameter and points off the circle. Floating-point evidence for finitely many points; the proof is in the lesson.

experiments.title: SSA: zero, one or two triangles
experiments.summary: Counts, with exact rational arithmetic, the triangles with given AB = c, BC = a and angle A, for 4,000 integer cases and ten rational directions of the ray AB. It exhibits two non-congruent triangles with the same SSA data and checks the classical rule for when this happens on every case of the grid. A finite check of the rule; the lesson proves it.

experiments.title: Forty primes in a row, then a counterexample
experiments.summary: Tests n^2 + n + 41 for primality (exact trial division) for n = 0 to 39, where every value is prime, then finds the first failure at n = 40, where the value is 41 * 41. Forty confirming cases were evidence, not proof; one counterexample settles the question.

experiments.title: Exact versus numerical: 0.1 + 0.2 and the square root of 2
experiments.summary: Compares 0.1 + 0.2 in floating point with exact fractions, shows how rounding error accumulates when 0.1 is added 10000 times in float64 and float32, and computes the square root of 2 by Newton's method (approximate) and with sympy.sqrt(2) (exact). Numerical results are approximations whose error must be measured; exact and symbolic results involve no rounding.

experiments.title: Counterexample searches with stated bounds
experiments.summary: Searches all fifth-power equations a^5+b^5+c^5+d^5 = e^5 with e <= 150 and finds Lander and Parkin's counterexample to Euler's conjecture; finds the first x (26861) where primes 1 mod 4 overtake primes 3 mod 4; compares pi(x) with li(x) up to 10^6; and computes exactly where the Borwein sinc-integral pattern fails. Exhaustive only up to the bounds.

experiments.title: PSLQ rediscovers the BBP formula for pi
experiments.summary: Runs the PSLQ integer-relation algorithm on pi and eight BBP-type sums computed to 60 digits, recovering pi = 4S1 - 2S4 - S5 - S6, rechecked at 100 digits. Shows a spurious relation at low precision and a PSLQ lower bound when no relation is found, then extracts hexadecimal digits of pi at position 5001 with the BBP formula and checks them against exact integer arithmetic. Numerical evidence; the proof is in the lesson.

experiments.title: Compound interest, the number e, and logarithm tables
experiments.summary: Computes (1 + 1/n)^n for n = 1 ... 10^6 and compares the error with the prediction e/(2n); computes partial sums of 1/k! with exact fractions; and checks ln(xy) = ln x + ln y numerically, the principle of logarithm tables. Floating-point evidence, with error estimates.

experiments.title: Doubling against powers: when does 2^n win for good?
experiments.summary: Finds, with exact integers, the point from which 2^n > n^k for k = 2, 3, 5, 10, and combines the search with an induction step (the ratio (1 + 1/n)^k < 2) so that the finite check proves the inequality for all larger n. Also computes the thickness of a sheet of paper folded 42 times.

experiments.title: Left to right, or multiplication first?
experiments.summary: Evaluates expressions both strictly left to right (like a simple calculator) and with the order-of-operations convention, using exact fractions. For all 11664 expressions a op b op c with digits 1-9 and the four operations it shows exactly when the two readings can disagree: when + or - is followed by x or /.

experiments.title: Which rule made this table?
experiments.summary: Tries all 121 rules 'multiply by a, then add b' (a, b from 0 to 10) against the rows of the table 1 -> 4, 2 -> 7, 3 -> 10, 4 -> 13. One row fits five rules, two rows fit one; a rule of another kind, n x n + 3, also fits two rows. Then it undoes 3 x n + 1 to find inputs from outputs and checks them forwards.

experiments.title: Divisibility tests, checked and broken
experiments.summary: Checks the last-digit tests for 2, 5 and 10, the digit-sum tests for 3 and 9 and the alternating-sum test for 11 on every number below 100,000, and finds the smallest counterexamples to two false shortcuts: a digit-sum test for 7 and a last-digit test for 4. Complete for these numbers; the lesson gives the proofs.

experiments.title: Sieving primes and growing factor trees
experiments.summary: Runs the sieve of Eratosthenes to 100 and 10,000, checks that stopping at the square root gives the same primes, factors every n from 2 to 5,000 along two different factor trees and finds the same primes each time (evidence for unique factorisation, not a proof), and factors Euclid's numbers to show their prime factors are new.

experiments.title: Galois groups seen through factorisation modulo primes
experiments.summary: Factors four polynomials modulo all suitable primes below 2000 and tallies the degree patterns, which are cycle types of Frobenius elements. The frequencies approach the proportions predicted by the Galois groups Z/2, S3, (Z/2)^2 and S5 (Chebotarev's density theorem). Each factorisation is exact; the agreement of frequencies is statistical evidence.

experiments.title: How many irreducible polynomials? Sieve versus Gauss
experiments.summary: Finds all monic irreducible polynomials of small degree over F_2, F_3 and F_5 by sieving out products, and compares the counts with Gauss's formula (1/n) sum mu(d) p^(n/d), which follows from X^(p^n) - X being the product of the irreducibles of degree dividing n. Exhaustive for the cases shown.

experiments.title: Truth in every structure with at most three elements
experiments.summary: Implements Tarski's satisfaction relation for formulas with one binary relation symbol, evaluates the axioms of equivalence relations, partial orders and linear orders on every relation on a set of at most three elements, counts models up to isomorphism, checks isomorphism invariance exhaustively, and separates the five partial orders on three points by four sentences.

experiments.title: Shortest programs, many answers, and fixing a bug
experiments.summary: Runs all 5,460 arrow programs of 1 to 6 cards, finds the shortest programs to each square reached and checks that their length is the across-plus-up distance and their number a binomial coefficient; then searches every one-instruction fix of a buggy floor-robot program. Exhaustive for these program lengths only.

experiments.title: A Cohen generic real escapes a list of ground-model reals
experiments.summary: Builds a descending sequence of Cohen conditions (finite binary strings) meeting the dense sets 'decide bit n' and 'disagree with x' for a list of reals x standing in for a countable ground model, and checks exactly that the result differs from every listed real; then checks that the filter of initial segments of a real misses a dense set. Finite stand-in only.

experiments.title: Model checking mutual exclusion: two flawed protocols and Peterson's
experiments.summary: Explores every reachable state of three two-process mutual-exclusion protocols by breadth-first search. It finds a shortest trace in which a naive protocol lets both processes into the critical section, a deadlock in a second protocol, and confirms mutual exclusion, deadlock freedom and AG EF crit for Peterson's algorithm (EF computed as a least fixed point). Exhaustive for these finite models only; fairness is not modelled.

experiments.title: Verification conditions for division by repeated subtraction
experiments.summary: Generates the verification conditions of a loop program from a weakest-precondition calculus, with SymPy doing the substitutions. The equational part of each condition is checked symbolically and the whole implication on every point of a box of integers (evidence for the box only). A too-weak invariant yields a condition with a counterexample, and random tests of the program are shown for contrast.

experiments.title: Images, composites and quantifiers on all small examples
experiments.summary: Checks on every function between sets of size at most 3 that images preserve intersections exactly for injective functions, that g o f injective forces f (but not g) to be injective, and on every relation between sets of size at most 3 that exists-forall implies forall-exists but not conversely, printing the smallest counterexamples.

experiments.title: A tiny proof checker for propositional logic
experiments.summary: Implements a checker for Hilbert-style proofs in implicational logic (axioms K and S, modus ponens), checks the five-line proof of p -> p, rejects a faulty proof with a precise error, and confirms by truth tables that every axiom instance tried and every proved formula is a tautology - evidence of soundness, not a proof of it.

experiments.title: A blueprint as a graph: ready items, critical path, cycles
experiments.summary: Treats the lesson's blueprint for Zagier's proof as a directed graph and computes a valid formalisation order (Kahn's algorithm), the items ready to formalise given those already done, the longest dependency chain, and a cycle in a deliberately circular variant. Exact graph computations; they say nothing about whether any lemma is true.

experiments.title: Zagier's involution, tested claim by claim
experiments.summary: Checks every claim of Zagier's one-sentence proof - no boundary cases, the map preserves S and is an involution, exactly one fixed point, |S| odd, the swap has a fixed point - for all primes p = 1 (mod 4) below 3000, and shows where the argument fails for composite n = 1 (mod 4). Exhaustive for these finitely many cases; the proof for all primes is in the lesson and in Lean.

experiments.title: Adding fractions: right rule, wrong rule, exact answers
experiments.summary: Using exact fractions, checks the rule a/b + c/d = (ad + cb)/(bd) on all 6,084 pairs of fractions in (0, 1] with denominators up to 12; the wrong rule (a + c)/(b + d) never gives the sum and always lands between the two fractions. Confirms the cross-multiplication test on 90,000 pairs and shows 0.1 + 0.2 != 0.3 in floating point. Complete for these cases only.

experiments.title: Decimals that stop and decimals that repeat
experiments.summary: Computes decimal expansions by long division, detecting the repeating block from a repeated remainder, for 1/2 to 1/20. Then checks, for all 4,950 fractions a/b with 1 <= a < b <= 100, that the decimal stops exactly when the lowest-terms denominator has no prime factors other than 2 and 5. Complete for these fractions; the lesson explains why the rule holds in general.

experiments.title: Eigenvalues of a compact operator, numerically
experiments.summary: Discretises the Green's operator of -u'' on (0, 1) by an N x N symmetric matrix and compares its eigenvalues with the exact 1/(k pi)^2: they agree to about 2e-6, the eigenvectors are orthonormal, and the eigenvalues accumulate only at 0. Exact computations show that differentiation has no bound and that sup and L^1 norms are inequivalent. Numerical evidence for one operator; the spectral theorem is proved in the lesson.

experiments.title: Evaluating an inverse function by bisection
experiments.summary: Evaluates the inverse of the strictly increasing function f(x) = x^3 + x by bisection with exact fractions, with a guaranteed error bound (width / 2^n), checks that swapped points lie on the inverse's graph, and shows that x^2 fails to be injective until its domain is restricted.

experiments.title: Moving graphs and splitting functions into even and odd parts
experiments.summary: Checks with exact fractions that points of y = f(x) move to points of y = a f(b(x - h)) + k by (x, y) -> (x/b + h, ay + k), shows that y = f(x - 2) moves the graph right, and splits several functions into even and odd parts, testing parity on a finite grid of rational points.

experiments.title: Telling groups apart with hom functors
experiments.summary: Counts homomorphisms Z/n -> G (elements with g^n = e) for the five groups of order 8 and for Z/4 x Z/4 and Z/2 x Q8, and counts homomorphisms Z x Z -> G (commuting pairs). Equal counts never prove two groups isomorphic; different counts prove they are not, because functors preserve isomorphisms. Exact computation on finite groups.

experiments.title: The figure eight: free group words and covering spaces
experiments.summary: Reduces words in the free group on a and b, the fundamental group of the figure eight; counts reduced words, shows ab and ba differ, and detects this with a homomorphism to S3. It then counts n-sheeted covering spaces as pairs of permutations: connected ones correspond to transitive pairs, giving 1, 3, 13, 71, 461 subgroups of index n = 1 to 5 and 1, 3, 7, 26 coverings up to isomorphism for n = 1 to 4.

experiments.title: Winding numbers by lifting loops to the real line
experiments.summary: Lifts sampled loops in the punctured plane to the real line by following the angle continuously, and compares the winding number with a separate midpoint-rule contour integral. It shows that the winding number is constant along a homotopy until the loop crosses 0, and that a cubic's image of circles winds 0 times for small and 3 times for large radii, forcing a root. Numerical evidence only.

experiments.title: Topological charge of U(1) lattice gauge fields on a torus
experiments.summary: Builds U(1) lattice gauge fields of prescribed charge k on a periodic N x N lattice, computes the plaquette angles and the integer charge Q = sum(theta_p) / 2 pi (a lattice first Chern number), and shows that Q is unchanged by random gauge transformations and by small noise, while large noise can change it. Numerical illustration of theorems.

experiments.title: Wilson loops, gauge invariance and the Aharonov-Bohm phase
experiments.summary: Builds a random SU(2) lattice gauge field and shows that a random gauge transformation changes holonomy matrices but not their traces (Wilson loops). Then builds a U(1) field that is flat except on one plaquette (a solenoid of flux Phi) and shows that loops in the field-free region acquire the phase exp(i w Phi), the same for two gauge-equivalent vector potentials. Numerical illustration of theorems.

experiments.title: Catenoids between two rings: minimal versus minimising
experiments.summary: Solves R = a cosh(h/a) for the catenoids spanning two coaxial rings, finds by bisection the critical ratio h/R = 0.6627... beyond which no catenoid exists and the ratio 0.5277... beyond which two flat discs have less area, and compares the areas of the thin catenoid, the fat catenoid and the discs: a minimal surface need not minimise area. Numerical, with closed-form areas and bisection to 1e-12.

experiments.title: Curve-shortening flow: area falls at rate 2 pi, shapes round off
experiments.summary: Discretises curve-shortening flow for a non-convex three-lobed curve with a 120-vertex polygon and explicit time steps. Compares the area with the exact law A(t) = A(0) - 2 pi t, tracks the isoperimetric ratio L^2/(4 pi A) towards 1 and the moment the curve becomes convex, as the Gage-Hamilton-Grayson theorem predicts. Numerical approximation with discretisation error.

experiments.title: Balls in Cayley graphs: polynomial and exponential growth
experiments.summary: Counts balls in Cayley graphs by breadth-first search: Z^2 (quadratic), the subgroup of SL(2, Z) generated by Sanov's matrices (exactly 2 * 3^r - 1 elements, as in a free group, up to radius 8) and the integer Heisenberg group (estimated growth degree near 4, as the Bass-Guivarc'h formula predicts). Exact counts on finite balls; the degree estimates are numerical.

experiments.title: Return probabilities of random walks: Z^2 versus the free group
experiments.summary: Computes the exact probability that simple random walk returns to its start after 2n steps on Z^2 (closed formula, checked against a direct count) and on the 4-regular tree, the Cayley graph of the free group F_2 (exact birth-death recursion). The n-th roots approach 1 and sqrt(3)/2, illustrating Kesten's amenability criterion; exact for finitely many n, the limits themselves are theorems.

experiments.title: Euler trails on every graph with five vertices
experiments.summary: Searches all trails in each of the 1024 simple graphs on five labelled vertices and confirms Euler's criterion for every connected one: an Euler circuit exists exactly when all degrees are even, an Euler trail exactly when 0 or 2 degrees are odd. Also shows that the Konigsberg multigraph has no Euler trail and builds an Euler circuit of K5 with Hierholzer's algorithm. Exhaustive for five vertices only.

experiments.title: Counting trees and sorting graphs by isomorphism
experiments.summary: Checks every set of n - 1 edges on n <= 7 labelled vertices: connected exactly when acyclic, and there are n^(n-2) labelled trees (Cayley's formula). Sorts the trees into isomorphism classes with a canonical code (1, 1, 1, 2, 3, 6, 11 classes), finds an isomorphism between a pentagon and a pentagram by trying all 120 bijections, and separates two graphs with equal degrees by connectedness. Small cases only.

experiments.title: Hall's marriage theorem and Konig's theorem, tested
experiments.summary: On 400 seeded random bipartite graphs with five vertices on each side, compares Hall's condition (all subsets) with augmenting-path matchings, and checks the deficiency version of Hall's theorem and Konig's theorem (maximum matching = minimum vertex cover, by brute force). Experimental evidence on small graphs only.

experiments.title: Ramsey numbers: exhaustive search for R(3, 3) and Erdos's bound
experiments.summary: Checks all 32768 red-blue colourings of K6 for monochromatic triangles (every one has at least two, as Goodman's theorem says), finds the 12 colourings of K5 with none, and tabulates the lower bounds for R(k, k) given by Erdos's probabilistic counting argument. The exhaustive part is a computer proof of R(3, 3) = 6, as far as the code is correct.

experiments.title: A journey graph: segment rates, averages and round trips
experiments.summary: Computes exact average rates of change on each segment of a cycling journey's distance-time table, classifies each segment as increasing, constant or decreasing, verifies the weighted-average rule for combining intervals, contrasts zero net change with the distance actually ridden, and compares round-trip average speeds with the mean of the two speeds.

experiments.title: A falling stone: average speeds over shrinking intervals
experiments.summary: For the idealised falling-stone model d(t) = 4.9 t^2, computes exact average speeds second by second, then over the intervals [2, 2 + h] for h = 1, 1/10, 1/100, 1/1000 and their negatives, checking each against the formula 19.6 + 4.9h. The values approach 19.6 m/s, a preview of instantaneous speed; finitely many h prove no limit.

experiments.title: Necklaces, bracelets and cubes: Burnside versus brute force
experiments.summary: Counts necklaces and bracelets with n <= 8 beads and colourings of a cube's faces in two ways: by Burnside's lemma (average number of fixed colourings, k to the number of cycles) and by brute-force enumeration of orbits. The two always agree here; the lemma's proof is in the lesson.

experiments.title: All subgroups of S3, D4, A4, S4 and C12
experiments.summary: Generates five permutation groups, finds every subgroup as an iterated join of cyclic subgroups, checks that each subgroup order divides the group order (Lagrange), counts normal subgroups, and exhibits the counterexample to the converse of Lagrange: A4 has order 12 but no subgroup of order 6. Exact and exhaustive for these groups only.

experiments.title: Gibbs overshoot, Fejer means and Parseval
experiments.summary: Samples the Fourier partial sums S_N of the square wave near its jump: the maximum stays near (2/pi) Si(pi) = 1.17898 as N grows, an overshoot of about 9% of the jump. The Fejer means stay below 1. Parseval gives the L^2 error of S_N, and the sum of 1/k^2 over odd k tends to pi^2/8. Sampled maxima for finitely many N: evidence, with the limits proved in the lesson.

experiments.title: Theta, Poisson summation and the uncertainty principle
experiments.summary: Checks Jacobi's identity theta(t) = t^(-1/2) theta(1/t), a consequence of Poisson summation, to floating-point accuracy for several t. Then computes the Heisenberg uncertainty ratio by numerical integration for a Gaussian (ratio 1, the extremal case), a two-sided exponential (ratio 2) and a tent function (ratio 6/5). Numerical checks of proved identities and inequalities.

experiments.title: Associahedra: bracketings, associators and the pentagon
experiments.summary: Enumerates all bracketings of n letters (n <= 7) and the graph of single associator moves, the 1-skeleton of the associahedron K_n. Checks Catalan counts, connectivity, the pentagon's paths of lengths 2 and 3, and that K_5 has 6 pentagons and 3 squares with V - E + F = 2. Exhaustive for these n; Mac Lane's coherence theorem covers every n.

experiments.title: Homology of glued squares and universal coefficients
experiments.summary: Builds the cellular chain complexes of the torus, Klein bottle, sphere and real projective plane from square gluing words, checks d1 d2 = 0, computes integral homology by Smith normal form and homology over F_2, F_3 and Q by ranks, and verifies the universal coefficient theorem and the Euler characteristic in each case. Exact computations for four complexes.

experiments.title: Tor and Ext of cyclic groups from resolutions
experiments.summary: For all 1 <= m, n <= 20 computes Tor_0, Tor_1, Hom and Ext^1 of Z/m and Z/n as kernels and cokernels of multiplication by m on Z/n, checks that each has gcd(m, n) elements, and recomputes Tor_1 from a second, non-minimal free resolution of Z/m to confirm independence of the resolution. Exhaustive in that range; the lesson proves both facts.

experiments.title: Hopf fibres are linked circles
experiments.summary: Samples fibres of the Hopf map S^3 -> S^2, checks numerically that the map is constant on each fibre, projects the fibres stereographically to R^3 and evaluates the Gauss linking integral for several pairs; it is 1 to about ten digits. Numerical evidence for the linking of Hopf fibres, which the lesson proves; it is not itself a proof.

experiments.title: Encode-decode for the circle: words, winding numbers, Z
experiments.summary: Models loops in the circle as words in loop and its inverse. Encoding by transport in the universal cover (successor and predecessor on Z) and decoding n as loop^n, it checks exhaustively for all 8190 non-empty words of length <= 12 that decode(encode(w)) is the free reduction of w and that encode is additive, then computes winding numbers of plane loops numerically. A finite model, not the type-theoretic proof.

experiments.title: The diagonal lemma, computed with Goedel numbers
experiments.summary: Goedel-numbers strings by a bijective base-k code, computes the diagonal function diag, and checks exactly that the sentence G = phi(code of phi) built from phi(x) = P(diag(x)) satisfies diag(code phi) = code G. Evaluates such fixed points for decidable P and shows that the liar sentence has no consistent truth value. Illustrates the mechanism only: no provability is computed.

experiments.title: Listing the theorems of the MIU system
experiments.summary: Enumerates every theorem of Hofstadter's MIU system reachable through strings of at most 16 symbols, checks the mod-3 invariant on each, and confirms the characterisation of theorems for all strings of at most 7 symbols. Shows that theorems are computably enumerable while MU's non-derivability needs a proof (the invariant), not a longer search.

experiments.title: Horn filling in nerves of small categories
experiments.summary: Enumerates every 2- and 3-dimensional horn in the nerves of four small categories (a poset, a monoid with an idempotent, the group Z/3, the walking isomorphism) and counts fillers: inner horns fill uniquely, outer horns fill in groupoids and may fail or fill non-uniquely otherwise. Exhaustive for these categories and dimensions only.

experiments.title: Repetition codes, the Hamming code and channel capacity
experiments.summary: Computes the capacity 1 - H(p) of binary symmetric channels and the exact error probabilities of repetition codes (rate 1/n) and of the Hamming (7, 4) code (rate 4/7), then simulates 20,000 Hamming blocks with syndrome decoding. Shows the trade-off that Shannon's theorem resolves: good codes need not have rate tending to zero.

experiments.title: Huffman coding and the entropy bound on a real sentence
experiments.summary: Builds a Huffman code for the character frequencies of Article 1 of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, checks Kraft's equality and the bounds H <= L < H + 1, compares fixed-length and Shannon codes, and shows that coding pairs of characters reduces the overhead per character. Exact rational arithmetic (entropies shown rounded) for this one text and its i.i.d. model.

experiments.title: Typical sequences: the asymptotic equipartition property
experiments.summary: For Bernoulli(0.2) sequences of length n up to 2,000, computes exactly (via binomial coefficients, in logarithms) the probability of the typical set and the base-2 logarithm of its size, compared with n H and with n. The typical set's probability approaches 1 while it contains a vanishing fraction of all sequences.

experiments.title: Hunting for inverses in the integers and the rationals
experiments.summary: Searches a finite window of integers for additive and multiplicative inverses (every additive inverse is found; multiplicative ones only for 1 and -1), then checks exactly with fractions that every non-zero rational has an inverse. A finite search is experimental evidence; the short size argument printed at the end is what proves that no other integer has a multiplicative inverse.

experiments.title: Difference quotients: exact, numerical and symbolic
experiments.summary: Shows with exact fractions that the difference quotient of x^2 at a is 2a + h; tabulates floating-point forward and central quotients of sin at 1 against cos 1 for h = 1e-1 ... 1e-13, where rounding error eventually wins; and lets SymPy compute the limit and the derivative of x^n symbolically.

experiments.title: Riemann sums for the parabola, exactly
experiments.summary: Computes left, right and midpoint Riemann sums of x^2 on [0, 1] in exact rational arithmetic, confirms the closed form (n + 1)(2n + 1)/(6n^2) for every n up to 200 and the exact errors 1/(2n) + 1/(6n^2) and -1/(12n^2), compares with the antiderivative x^3/3 (SymPy), and shows signed area for sin on [0, 2 pi] numerically.

experiments.title: A toy proof checker for natural-number addition
experiments.summary: Implements a checker for equational proofs from the rules a + 0 = a and a + S(b) = S(a + b): it accepts 2 + 2 = 4, rejects a wrong step, finds that 0 + n is stuck when n is a variable (so induction is needed), checks 0 + k = k by computation for k up to 100, and checks both cases of the induction proof.

experiments.title: Counting compatible maps into a candidate product
experiments.summary: For A = {red, blue} and B = {1, 2, 3}, counts, for every pair of functions f : X -> A, g : X -> B, the maps h : X -> P compatible with them, for four candidates P. Pairs and a 6-element set of numbers give exactly one h every time; two fakes give 0 or 4. Exhaustive for the small sets X tested, not a proof for all X.

experiments.title: Pointwise Kan extensions of finite sets: colimits and limits
experiments.summary: Computes left and right Kan extensions of functors into finite sets by their pointwise formulas (colimits by union-find, limits as compatible families): Lan and Ran along a map of finite posets give coproducts and products, and Kan extension along BH -> BS3 gives induced and coinduced H-sets of sizes [G:H]|X| and |X|^[G:H]. Exact for these finite cases only; the general theorems are proved in the lesson.

experiments.title: Fox colourings and knot determinants
experiments.summary: Builds the colouring equations 2x = y + z of six knot diagrams from their PD codes, counts Fox p-colourings for p = 3, 5, 7 by linear algebra mod p (cross-checked by brute force on small cases) and computes each determinant exactly. It shows tricolourability matches 3 | det, and that 4_1 and 5_1 have the same counts although they are different knots. Exact, for these diagrams.

experiments.title: Kauffman bracket and Jones polynomial from PD codes
experiments.summary: Computes the Kauffman bracket state sum and the writhe of planar diagram codes, and from them the Jones polynomial of the trefoil, its mirror, the figure-eight knot and the knots 5_1, 5_2 and 6_1. It checks that a kink multiplies the bracket by -A^3 but leaves V unchanged, that V(1) = 1, and that the trefoil's V differs from its mirror's. Exact, for these diagrams only.

experiments.title: Church numerals, recursion and non-termination in the λ-calculus
experiments.summary: Parses named λ-terms into de Bruijn indices and reduces them with capture-avoiding substitution. Normal-order reduction computes Church arithmetic (2+3, 2*3, 2^3), booleans, Kleene's predecessor and 3! via the Y combinator, counting β-steps; Omega exhausts any fuel, and K I Omega normalises under normal order but not applicative order. Exact results for these terms only, not proofs of the general theorems.

experiments.title: Church–Rosser on every small λ-term: an exhaustive check
experiments.summary: Enumerates all 38,438 λ-terms with at most one free variable up to size 10, builds each term's full β-reduction graph (all redexes, all orders; graphs over 200 terms are set aside) and checks that any two reducts have a common reduct and that no term reaches two normal forms. Also counts terms that normalise yet have infinite reductions. Exhaustive for these finitely many terms only; the theorem is proved in Lean.

experiments.title: An elliptic curve and its modular form; Ramanujan's tau
experiments.summary: Counts points of the elliptic curve 11a1 modulo every prime p < 400 and compares the traces a_p with the coefficients of q prod (1 - q^n)^2 (1 - q^11n)^2; checks Hecke multiplicativity of those coefficients and of Ramanujan's tau(n), Ramanujan's congruence mod 691 and Deligne's bound, all for n <= 400. Exact finite checks of known theorems.

experiments.title: Reciprocity laws: quadratic, cyclotomic and a modular form
experiments.summary: Checks quadratic reciprocity for all pairs of odd primes below 200, verifies the congruence splitting laws of x^2 + 1 and x^2 - 5, shows that no congruence mod 23 decides how x^3 - x - 1 factors while the modular form eta(z)eta(23z) does (all p < 2000), and compares splitting frequencies with Chebotarev's densities. Finite checks of theorems.

experiments.title: Hereditarily finite sets: V_omega in Ackermann's coding
experiments.summary: Codes hereditarily finite sets as natural numbers (m is in n iff bit m of n is 1), computes ranks, checks that V_k is exactly the codes below |V_k| for k <= 5, that pairing, union and power set stay inside V_omega but leave each V_k, and computes |V_k|. Exact finite checks illustrating, by analogy, why inaccessible kappa make V_kappa a model of ZFC.

experiments.title: Laver tables and the period of their first row
experiments.summary: Builds the Laver tables A_n (n <= 9), checks left self-distributivity exhaustively for n <= 5, and computes the period of the first row (1, 1, 2, 4, 4, 8, 8, 8, 8, 16). Laver proved from the large cardinal axiom I3 that this period tends to infinity; exact computation for small n only, which says nothing about that limit.

experiments.title: The matrix exponential: rotations, commutators and SL(2, R)
experiments.summary: Computes matrix exponentials numerically: exp of a skew-symmetric matrix is a rotation given by Rodrigues' formula; det exp X = e^(tr X); the group commutator of exp(tX) and exp(tY) is I + t^2 [X, Y] + O(t^3); and random samples of exp(sl(2, R)) never have trace below -2, so diag(-2, -1/2) is not an exponential. Numerical and sampled evidence.

experiments.title: Representations of sl(2) and the roots of sl(3)
