experiments.summary: Builds the irreducible representations V_n of sl(2, C) for n = 0..8 with exact integer matrices, checks the bracket relations and that the Casimir acts as n(n+2)/2, decomposes V_m (x) V_n by weights into V_(m+n) + ... + V_|m-n|, and computes the roots of sl(3) as eigenvalues of ad(H), recovering the hexagon A2 and its Cartan matrix. Exact.

experiments.title: Limits and colimits of finite sets, computed two ways
experiments.summary: Computes limits of small diagrams of finite sets as compatible families and as equalisers of two maps between products, and checks they agree; computes colimits as quotients of disjoint unions with a union-find; and counts reduced words in Z/2 * Z/3 to compare it with the 5-element coproduct of the underlying sets. Exact for these finite diagrams.

experiments.title: The p-adic integers as compatible towers of residues
experiments.summary: Builds compatible towers x_n mod p^n representing -1 and 1/3 in Z_2 and Z_5 and a square root of -1 in Z_5 (Hensel lifting), checks compatibility and levelwise arithmetic, and counts solutions of x^2 = -1 and x^2 = 2 modulo 5^n for n <= 6. Exact for the levels computed; that the towers determine p-adic integers is the inverse-limit theorem.

experiments.title: Diagonalisable or not: 625 matrices and the Fibonacci numbers
experiments.summary: Sorts all 625 integer 2 x 2 matrices with entries from -2 to 2 into real-diagonalisable, complex-only, scalar and defective, using the discriminant of the characteristic polynomial; then diagonalises the Fibonacci matrix with SymPy and verifies Binet's formula exactly for n <= 40, and exhibits a defective (non-diagonalisable) matrix.

experiments.title: Exact Gaussian elimination and rank-nullity
experiments.summary: Row-reduces matrices with exact fractions, reads off pivots, rank and a basis of the null space, and checks that every basis vector solves Ax = 0 and that rank + nullity = n. Run on the lesson's worked example and on 300 random integer matrices of prescribed rank: exact arithmetic, but only finitely many cases.

experiments.title: Linear equations: exact solutions and inequality flips
experiments.summary: Solves the lesson's equations a*x + b = c*x + d exactly with fractions via the standard form (a - c)x = d - b and checks each answer by substitution; counts, for all 2401 equations with coefficients in -3..3, how many of the values -5..5 solve each one (never exactly two); and tests the inequality-reversal rule on 10,000 random fractions.

experiments.title: Linear tables and systems: one, none or infinitely many
experiments.summary: Tests tables of values for a constant slope with exact fractions and recovers y = mx + b; solves the lesson's systems of two equations by elimination and checks the answers; and classifies all 15,625 systems with coefficients in -2..2 into one solution, no solution or infinitely many, checking every unique solution by substitution.

experiments.title: Counterexample hunting up to 10000
experiments.summary: Tests five claims about every whole number on all numbers up to 10000, counting fitting examples and counterexamples. Three claims are refuted by a counterexample (one only after ten successes); Goldbach's conjecture and 'double n is even' have none in range. A counterexample is a disproof; finding none is not a proof.

experiments.title: Truth tables: and, or, not in every row
experiments.summary: Prints the truth tables of and, inclusive or, exclusive or and not for two statements, checks De Morgan's laws and double negation in all four rows, and finds the single row where inclusive and exclusive or differ. Every case is checked, so for these laws the check is a complete proof.

experiments.title: Column addition: a loop with a carry
experiments.summary: Runs the column-addition loop step by step for 368 + 275, then compares it with ordinary addition for all 40000 pairs of numbers below 200 and 2000 seeded random pairs with up to 12 digits. Every answer agrees, no column total exceeds 19 and no carry exceeds 1. Exhaustive for small numbers; a sample for large ones.

experiments.title: Loops that close, loops that stop, and one that never stops
experiments.summary: Runs turtle loops 'repeat n times: forward 1, turn right a degrees' for squares, triangles, hexagons and a star, reporting the distance from the start (floating point) and the total turning. Then runs three 'repeat until' loops, one of which never meets its stopping condition and is cut off after 1000 steps.

experiments.title: Intersection forms: E8, Rokhlin, Freedman and Donaldson
experiments.summary: Computes exactly the rank, determinant, signature (by rational diagonalisation) and parity of unimodular forms including E8, E8 + E8 and the K3 form, and reads off what the theorems of Freedman, Rokhlin and Donaldson say about topological and smooth 4-manifolds with these forms; also |det| of linking matrices, the order of H_1 after surgery. Exact linear algebra; the topology is cited.

experiments.title: Lens spaces: homeomorphism versus homotopy, by arithmetic
experiments.summary: Applies the classification criteria for lens spaces L(p, q) (homeomorphic iff q' = +-q^(+-1) mod p; homotopy equivalent iff qq' = +-n^2 mod p) to every p up to 15, counting the classes and listing the pairs that are homotopy equivalent but not homeomorphic, and evaluates the torsion moduli that distinguish L(7, 1) from L(7, 2). Exact and exhaustive for the arithmetic; the topology is cited, not computed.

experiments.title: Convergence to equilibrium, eigenvalues and Doeblin's bound
experiments.summary: Solves pi P = pi exactly for a 3-state weather chain, then tracks the total-variation distance between mu P^n and pi: it decays like |lambda_2|^n and stays below Doeblin's bound (1 - k delta)^n. A periodic two-state chain oscillates forever, while its lazy version converges. Floating-point powers of a small matrix; the convergence theorem itself is proved in the lesson.

experiments.title: Gambler's ruin: exact first-step analysis versus simulation
experiments.summary: Solves the first-step equations for the probability of reaching N before 0 and for the expected duration exactly (fractions), confirms the closed forms i/N, (1 - r^i)/(1 - r^N) and i(N - i), and compares with 4,000 simulated games for a fair coin and for p = 18/38. Exact for the listed cases; the simulation is statistical evidence.

experiments.title: Polya's theorem: return probabilities in one, two and three dimensions
experiments.summary: Computes P(S_2n = 0) for simple random walk in dimensions 1, 2 and 3 and the partial sums of the expected number of returns: they diverge like sqrt(n) and log(n) in dimensions 1 and 2 and converge in dimension 3. A seeded simulation of 1,000 walks of 1,000 steps shows how many return. Finite computations illustrate, but cannot prove, divergence or convergence.

experiments.title: Logistic map: period doubling, Feigenbaum ratios and Lyapunov exponents
experiments.summary: Iterates the logistic map to find attractor periods (1, 2, 4, 8, chaos, a period-3 window), computes superstable parameters by Newton's method and the ratios of their gaps, which approach Feigenbaum's constant 4.669, and estimates Lyapunov exponents, showing exponential divergence of nearby orbits at r = 4. Floating-point evidence about finitely many iterates.

experiments.title: Lotka-Volterra: conserved quantity, Euler versus RK4, cycle averages
experiments.summary: Integrates the Lotka-Volterra predator-prey equations with Euler's method and with RK4 and monitors the conserved quantity V: Euler drifts outward, RK4 conserves V closely. Measures the period of the cycle and the average prey and predator populations over one period, which match the equilibrium (c/d, a/b). Floating-point numerical evidence.

experiments.title: SIR epidemics: Runge-Kutta solutions and the final-size relation
experiments.summary: Integrates the SIR model with RK4 for several values of R0 and compares the simulated attack rate and peak with the final-size relation s = exp(-R0(1 - s)) and the peak formula 1 - (1 + ln R0)/R0, tracks the conserved quantity S + I - ln(S)/R0, and contrasts the attack rate with the herd immunity threshold 1 - 1/R0 (overshoot). Numerical evidence for one model.

experiments.title: Blueprint check: forward references, circularity, conditional results
experiments.summary: Takes the dependency graph of a short expository note, with each item marked proved, cited, conjectured or a definition, and computes forward references in the written order, a valid order by topological sorting, circular dependencies, and which results are only conditional because they depend on a conjecture. Exact for the data; it does not check proofs.

experiments.title: Linting LaTeX: environments, references, macros and style flags
experiments.summary: Checks a draft and a revised LaTeX fragment for unbalanced environments, references to missing labels, undefined macros, sentences that start with a formula and words like 'clearly'. The analysis of the given text is exact, but these are mechanical style checks: they cannot detect mathematical errors.

experiments.title: The matrix exponential: rotations, determinants and the bracket
experiments.summary: Sums the exponential series (with scaling and squaring) to check that exp(theta J) is a rotation, that exp of a skew-symmetric matrix lies in SO(3), that det(exp X) = e^(tr X) for seeded random matrices, and that exp(tX)exp(tY) differs from exp(t(X+Y)) at order t^2, with the commutator term [X, Y]/2 removing that error. Floating-point evidence.

experiments.title: Unit quaternions as rotations, in exact arithmetic
experiments.summary: Multiplies quaternions with rational coordinates exactly, builds the rotation matrix of v -> q v q*, and verifies orthogonality, determinant 1, rho(-q) = rho(q), the homomorphism property and non-commutativity; then checks exhaustively that the 24 Hurwitz units form a group mapping two-to-one onto the 12 rotations of a tetrahedron.

experiments.title: Borel-Cantelli: events that keep happening, and events that stop
experiments.summary: Exact expected counts of independent events with P(A_n) = 1/n and P(B_n) = 1/n^2 in dyadic blocks (about ln 2 per block versus a geometrically shrinking amount), plus seeded simulations of five runs up to n = 2^16 showing the late occurrences of each. The simulation is statistical evidence for a finite horizon only; the almost-sure statements are the Borel-Cantelli lemmas proved in the lesson.

experiments.title: The CLT through characteristic functions
experiments.summary: Computes the characteristic function cos(t/sqrt(n))^n of a normalised sum of n fair +-1 coins on a grid in [-3, 3] and its distance from exp(-t^2/2) for n up to 10^4, showing the 1/n decay predicted by the Taylor expansion, then the exact binomial CDF error, which decays like 1/sqrt(n). Floating-point numerical evidence on finite grids only.

experiments.title: Polya's urn: a martingale with a random limit
experiments.summary: Computes exactly the distribution of red balls in Polya's urn after n draws (uniform on 1..n+1) and checks the martingale identity E[M_(n+1) | R_n = r] = M_n with fractions for every r and n <= 30. A seeded simulation of 1000 urns shows each fraction settling and the limits spreading out uniformly. The exact part is a finite check; the convergence is Doob's theorem.

experiments.title: The Cantor set: uncountable but of measure zero
experiments.summary: Computes the stages C_n of the Cantor set exactly with fractions: 2^n intervals of total length (2/3)^n, so the Cantor set has outer measure at most (2/3)^n for every n. Checks that 1/4 lies in every stage computed without being an endpoint, and that distinct 0/1 strings give distinct points (the injection behind uncountability). Finite stages only; the limiting statements are proved in the lesson.

experiments.title: Limits and integrals: four sequences of functions
experiments.summary: Computes exact integrals and point values for four sequences: escaping mass, a travelling bump, x^n on [0, 1] and the typewriter sequence. The first two are counterexamples to swapping limit and integral without a dominating function; the typewriter converges in L^1 yet its values at x = 1/3 keep returning to 1. Finitely many terms are computed; the limiting behaviour is proved in the lesson.

experiments.title: Units, gaps and overlaps: measuring a pencil in paper clips
experiments.summary: Measures six objects in three units exactly, checks that a smaller unit never gives a smaller count for every whole length up to 100 cm and every pair of units up to 20 cm, then simulates 1,000 careless measurements of a 15 cm pencil with seeded random gaps or overlaps. The simulation is experimental evidence; the lesson explains why gaps can never raise the count and overlaps can never lower it.

experiments.title: Eliminating a quantifier in dense linear orders
experiments.summary: Implements the elimination of Ex from conjunctions of order atoms in a dense linear order without endpoints, then compares it with a direct witness search in Q on 2000 random formulas (exact fractions). The same elimination fails in Z, and the program finds such counterexamples. Random tests support, but do not prove, correctness.

experiments.title: Ehrenfeucht-Fraisse games on finite linear orders
experiments.summary: Solves the k-round Ehrenfeucht-Fraisse game on finite linear orders of sizes m and n by exhaustive game-tree search (k <= 3, sizes up to 10) and checks the rule 'Duplicator wins iff m = n or m, n >= 2^k - 1'. By the Ehrenfeucht-Fraisse theorem this certifies which pairs agree on all sentences of quantifier rank <= k, but only for the sizes searched.

experiments.title: A perfect fit that predicts nonsense
experiments.summary: Fits a line, Newton's cooling law and an exact-fit degree-7 polynomial to eight synthetic, slightly noisy temperature readings, then compares their predictions beyond the data with the known true curve. The exact fit has zero error on the data and absurd forecasts. One seeded example.

experiments.title: Linear or exponential? Forecasting world population
experiments.summary: Fits linear and exponential models by least squares to approximate UN estimates of world population for 1950-1980, forecasts 1990-2020 and compares with the later estimates. Neither model survives validation: the growth rate itself changed. Numerical evidence about one data set.

experiments.title: Cycles of remainders: powers and calendars
experiments.summary: Finds the repeating cycles of 2^k, 3^k and 7^k modulo 10 and of 2^k modulo 7, predicts the last digit of 7^2026 from its cycle and checks it with exact arithmetic, and steps calendar cycles day by day until they realign (60 for 10 stems and 12 branches, 18980 days for the Maya 260- and 365-day counts), matching the least common multiple.

experiments.title: Partners and zero products on every clock up to 30
experiments.summary: Checks the reduce-first rules for sums and products for all a, b below 120 and n up to 30, then builds every multiplication table modulo n for n = 2 to 30: the remainders with a multiplicative partner are exactly those sharing no factor with n, and zero products appear exactly when n is not prime. Exhaustive for these n only; the lesson proves the rules.

experiments.title: Jordan blocks from invariant factors over Q[x]
experiments.summary: Computes the invariant factors of the Q[x]-module defined by a matrix from the gcds of minors of xI - A, predicts the Jordan blocks from the prime-power factors, and compares with sympy's jordan_form for four matrices, including two nilpotent matrices with the same characteristic and different module structure. Exact symbolic checks of examples, not a proof.

experiments.title: Smith normal form and the classification of abelian groups
experiments.summary: Reduces integer relation matrices to Smith normal form, reads off the abelian group they present, checks the divisibility chain and the determinantal-divisor identity on every 2 x 2 matrix with entries in [-3, 3] and on 300 random 3 x 3 matrices, and counts abelian groups of order n <= 100 in two independent ways. Exact arithmetic; the lesson proves the structure theorem for every PID.

experiments.title: Counting algebras for the maybe, power-set and list monads
experiments.summary: Searches every candidate structure map on sets with at most 3 elements: maybe-algebras are base points, power-set algebras are complete lattices (all chains this small), and among the 243 unital operations on 3 elements the list-algebra laws hold exactly for the associative ones. A fake monad (mu = intersection) breaks a unit law.

experiments.title: Kleisli composition for the distribution monad
experiments.summary: Computes Kleisli composition for the finite distribution monad from eta and mu, and checks with exact fractions that it equals the product of stochastic matrices, that the Kleisli laws hold, and that expectation satisfies the algebra laws (the tower property) - on 200 seeded random kernels, which is evidence, not proof.

experiments.title: A braided but not symmetric R-matrix
experiments.summary: With SymPy and a symbolic parameter q, verifies that the U_q(sl_2) R-matrix on C^2 (x) C^2 satisfies the braid (Yang-Baxter) relation and the Hecke relation, reduces to the swap at q = 1, and squares to the identity only when q^2 = 1 - a braiding that is not symmetric.

experiments.title: Pentagons, associahedra and a twisted associator
experiments.summary: Builds the associahedron graphs (bracketings and associator moves) for up to six objects, checks the 3-cocycle (pentagon) condition for the carry cochain on Z/n for n up to 6, and verifies that all paths between bracketings of five graded objects carry the same twist - while a naive twist fails both tests. Exhaustive, exact, finite.

experiments.title: Green's theorem: circulation versus integrated curl
experiments.summary: Computes the circulation of a planar vector field around circles (by the trapezoid rule in the angle) and the double integral of its curl over the discs (midpoint rule in polar coordinates). For a smooth field both are 3 pi / 2; for the vortex field around the origin they are 2 pi and 0, showing why Green's theorem needs F to be C^1 on the whole disc.

experiments.title: Lagrange multipliers solved exactly
experiments.summary: Uses SymPy to solve the Lagrange system grad f = lambda grad g, g = c exactly for three constrained problems (xy on a circle, the largest box of given surface area, the nearest point of a plane), lists every critical point with its value, and checks the multiplier equations. Exact, but only as reliable as SymPy's solver, which finds candidates; existence of an extremum needs the separate arguments in the lesson.

experiments.title: Polar coordinates and the Jacobian factor r
experiments.summary: Integrates exp(-(x^2 + y^2)) over discs by a Cartesian midpoint grid, by polar coordinates with the Jacobian factor r, and by polar coordinates without it, against the exact value pi (1 - exp(-R^2)). Forgetting r gives wrong answers. It also checks numerically that the one-dimensional Gaussian integral is close to sqrt(pi).

experiments.title: Invariant pairings: when could V be naturally isomorphic to V*?
experiments.summary: Counts non-degenerate bilinear forms on F_p^n invariant under all of GL_n(F_p), for p = 2, 3, 5 and n <= 3, by exhaustive search tested on generators of GL_n(F_p). They exist only in a few tiny cases (lines over F_2 and F_3, the plane over F_2). Also counts the invertible maps that preserve the dot product. Exact for these cases only.

experiments.title: Natural binary operations on finite sets: symmetry versus naturality
experiments.summary: Enumerates every table X x X -> X on sets of sizes 2 and 3 and keeps those commuting with all bijections, then those commuting with all self-maps. On three elements, symmetry allows three operations but naturality only the two projections; a non-injective map refutes the third. Exhaustive for these sizes only; the lesson's proof covers all sets.

experiments.title: One-stroke figures: exhaustive search versus Euler's rule
experiments.summary: Counts the degree of every dot in seven small figures, including the house puzzle and the seven bridges of Konigsberg, and searches every route that uses each line once. The search settles each figure for certain and agrees with Euler's odd-dot rule on all seven; it does not prove the rule for figures it has not tried.

experiments.title: Fewest roads or fewest kilometres? Shortest routes
experiments.summary: Lists every route from home to the market on a five-place road map with its number of roads and its length, showing that the route with fewest roads (13 km) is not the shortest (9 km). Dijkstra's method finds the same 9 km without listing every route. Exact for this map only.

experiments.title: Girard's theorem: angle excess equals area on the sphere
experiments.summary: For several spherical triangles, compares the angle excess with the area estimated by Monte Carlo sampling of 200,000 random points (with standard error) and with an exact closed formula, and checks the spherical law of cosines. Agreement within sampling error is evidence for Girard's theorem, which the lesson proves.

experiments.title: Hyperbolic triangles: angle defect, area and Moebius invariance
experiments.summary: Computes the angles of hyperbolic triangles in the upper half-plane by the law of cosines and, independently, from tangent directions; compares the defect with the Monte Carlo area (integral of dx dy / y^2); checks that random Moebius maps preserve lengths and angles; and shows the defect approaching pi as the triangle approaches an ideal triangle.

experiments.title: Closing in on the square root of 2 with fractions
experiments.summary: Runs the Babylonian iteration x -> (x + 2/x)/2 (from above) and the map q -> (2q + 2)/(q + 2) (from below) in exact fractions, checks that the lower terms lie in the Dedekind cut of sqrt(2) and the upper ones do not, and watches the gap shrink: two equivalent Cauchy sequences of rationals with no rational limit. Finite and exact; limits are left to the proofs.

experiments.title: Well-definedness tested on every small representative
experiments.summary: For integer pairs (a, b) ~ (c, d) iff a + d = c + b, and fraction pairs (a, b) ~ (c, d) iff ad = cb, checks every small choice of representatives: the lesson's addition and multiplication respect the relations; the componentwise product of integer pairs and the mediant of fractions do not (counterexamples printed). Also shows fraction equality over Z/6Z failing to be transitive.

experiments.title: Conditioning, pivoting and least squares in floating point
experiments.summary: Solves Hilbert systems and compares the error with kappa(H) times the unit roundoff; shows elimination without pivoting failing on [[1e-20, 1], [1, 1]] while partial pivoting succeeds; measures the growth factor 2^(n-1) on Wilkinson's matrix; and shows the normal equations breaking down on Lauchli's least-squares problem while QR works. Floating-point evidence.

experiments.title: One-step ODE methods: order, stiffness and rounding
experiments.summary: Measures the observed order of Euler (1), Heun (2) and classical RK4 (4) on y' = y; shows explicit Euler exploding on the stiff equation y' = -50 (y - cos t) when h > 2/50 while backward Euler stays accurate; and shows the total error of a difference quotient falling and then rising as h shrinks, because of rounding.

experiments.title: Truncation versus rounding, and smoothness in quadrature
experiments.summary: Measures the error of forward and central difference quotients for the derivative of sin at 1 as h shrinks from 1e-1 to 1e-13, showing the V shape where rounding error takes over; then measures trapezoid and Simpson errors for e^cos(x) on [0, 2 pi] (fast, because periodic) and for sqrt(x) on [0, 1] (slow, because not smooth at 0).

experiments.title: Machine epsilon and catastrophic cancellation
experiments.summary: Finds machine epsilon 2^-52 by repeated halving, shows the exact binary value stored for 0.1, and measures the relative error of (1 - cos x)/x^2 and of the quadratic formula's small root against accurate rearranged formulas, showing that cancellation of nearly equal numbers can lose every significant digit even though each operation is correctly rounded.

experiments.title: Bisection, Newton and secant: orders of convergence
experiments.summary: Solves x^2 = 2 in 50-digit decimal arithmetic by bisection, Newton's method and the secant method, printing the errors and estimated orders of convergence (about 1, 2 and 1.618). Then shows Newton's method converging only linearly at a double root and cycling forever for x^3 - 2x + 2 started at 0.

experiments.title: Gradient descent: rates, step sizes, Newton and least squares
experiments.summary: Runs gradient descent with step 1/L on a convex quadratic and compares the gap f(x_k) - f* with the proved O(1/k) bound and the geometric rate for strongly convex functions, tries step sizes beyond 2/L, shows Newton's method solving a quadratic in one step, and fits a line to seeded noisy data by gradient descent. Numerical evidence.

experiments.title: The simplex method and LP duality, in exact arithmetic
experiments.summary: Solves a small production linear program with the tableau simplex method in exact fractions, under Dantzig's and Bland's pivoting rules, prints the vertices visited, reads the dual solution (shadow prices) from the final tableau, verifies equal primal and dual values and complementary slackness, and detects an unbounded problem.

experiments.title: A census of all partial orders on small sets
experiments.summary: Tries every reflexive relation on sets of 1 to 4 elements, counting preorders, partial orders (1, 3, 19, 219), total orders (n!) and lattices, and checks on each partial order that a maximal element exists, and how often there is a greatest one. Exhaustive and exact for n <= 4 only.

experiments.title: Divisibility orders, lattices and a least fixed point
experiments.summary: Computes the Hasse diagram of divisibility on {1, ..., 12} and its maximal elements, checks exhaustively that the divisors of 60 form a lattice (meet gcd, join lcm) while {1, ..., 12} does not, and finds the least fixed point of a monotone map on subsets both by iteration from the empty set and as the meet of all pre-fixed points (Knaster-Tarski).

experiments.title: Euler and Runge-Kutta: convergence, blow-up, non-uniqueness
experiments.summary: Solves x' = x with Euler's method and RK4 and measures their orders (1 and 4); follows RK4 towards the blow-up of x' = x^2 at t = 1; and shows that for x' = sqrt|x| a method started at 0 stays at 0 while a start at 1e-12 tracks t^2/4. Floating-point evidence for these examples; the error theorems and Picard-Lindelof are the proofs.

experiments.title: Picard iteration: exact successive approximations
experiments.summary: Computes Picard iterates exactly with SymPy for x' = x, x' = t + x and x' = x^2 (all with x(0) = 1), compares them with the exact solutions, and shows the iterates for x' = x^2 agreeing with the series of 1/(1 - t) to higher and higher order. Exact symbolic computation of finitely many iterates; convergence is the Picard-Lindelof theorem.

experiments.title: Recovering interval decompositions of linear A_n
experiments.summary: Builds 200 seeded random representations of the linear quiver A_5 over F_7 as sums of interval modules, disguises them by random changes of basis, and recovers every multiplicity from ranks of composite maps by inclusion-exclusion. Exact modular arithmetic; evidence for these examples, while the lesson proves the classification and the rank formula in general.

experiments.title: Counting paths: dimensions of path algebras
experiments.summary: Counts paths in quivers with powers of the adjacency matrix: the dimension of the path algebra for linear A_n (n(n+1)/2), other orientations, D_4 and the Kronecker quiver, the Cartan matrix of path counts, and the growth of path counts for the one-loop and two-loop quivers, where the path algebra is k[x] or a free algebra. Exact counts for these quivers.

experiments.title: Predicting patterns, and patterns that fool us
experiments.summary: Predicts items of a repeating pattern from remainders and checks the shortcut against listing every item for 1,000 positions, finds the length of the repeating unit, compares 'add 2 each time' with '2 times the step', and shows three rules that all start 1, 2, 4 but continue differently, including circle regions (1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 31).

experiments.title: Fourier series: Gibbs overshoot and Parseval's identity
experiments.summary: Evaluates partial sums of the square-wave Fourier series at their first peak x = pi/(2n) and shows the peak tending to (2/pi) Si(pi) = 1.17898 instead of 1 (the Gibbs phenomenon), checks that the sums are 0 at the jump, and uses Parseval's identity for the sawtooth to approach sum 1/n^2 = pi^2/6 with error about 1/N. Numerical evidence.

experiments.title: Heat equation: series solution versus finite differences
experiments.summary: Solves u_t = u_xx on [0, pi] with zero boundary values and initial data x(pi - x), comparing the explicit finite-difference scheme with the Fourier sine series solution. For r = dt/dx^2 <= 1/2 the error is small and falls like dx^2 and the maximum principle holds; for r = 0.6 the highest mode grows each step and the scheme blows up.

experiments.title: Finite elements: Galerkin's method for -u'' = f
experiments.summary: Solves the weak form of -u'' = pi^2 sin(pi x), u(0) = u(1) = 0, by piecewise-linear finite elements for N = 4 to 64 elements. The energy error halves and the L^2 error quarters when h halves (rates 1 and 2), the nodal values agree with sin(pi x) to rounding error, and the stiffness matrix has a positive inverse (discrete maximum principle). Numerical evidence for one problem; Lax-Milgram and Cea's lemma explain it.

experiments.title: Heine-Borel by bisection: finite subcovers on demand
experiments.summary: Runs the bisection argument from the proof of Heine-Borel as an algorithm with exact fractions. For an open cover of [0, 1] it halts with a finite subcover; for the cover of (0, 1] by the intervals (1/n, 2) the left-most piece (0, 2^-d] is never covered, and the number of sets used grows with the depth d: (0, 1] is not compact. The runs illustrate the proof but are not themselves a proof.

experiments.title: All topologies on a small finite set
experiments.summary: Enumerates every family of subsets of an n-point set (n = 0 to 4) that satisfies the axioms of a topology, finding 1, 1, 4, 29 and 355 topologies, and counts how many are T0, T1 or Hausdorff and how many are connected. It shows open sets that are not closed and closed sets that are not open in the Sierpinski space. Exhaustive for these finite sets only.

experiments.title: Synthetic division and the remainder theorem
experiments.summary: Divides polynomials by x - a with exact fractions (synthetic division), confirms on 2,000 random cases that the remainder is p(a), and finds all rational roots of 2x^3 - 3x^2 - 11x + 6 with the rational root test. The random check is evidence for the cases tried; the lesson's proof covers all.

experiments.title: More roots than the degree? Polynomials modulo n
experiments.summary: Counts the roots of x^2 - 1 modulo n for n = 2..24 (n = 8 gives four roots of a quadratic), and checks exhaustively that every non-zero polynomial of degree at most 3 modulo 2, 3, 5 and 7 has at most degree-many roots, as the proof predicts when there are no zero divisors.

experiments.title: Chernoff bounds and balancing sets
experiments.summary: Compares the exact tail P(S >= a) of a sum of 100 random signs with Chebyshev's bound n/a^2, the Chernoff bound exp(-a^2/2n) and a seeded simulation, then colours 64 points at random and checks how often all of 64 random sets have imbalance at most sqrt(2n ln 2n), as the Chernoff-plus-union-bound argument predicts. Exact tails and statistical evidence.

experiments.title: Moser-Tardos: the local lemma as an algorithm
experiments.summary: Builds a random 5-CNF formula in which every clause meets at most 10 others, so the Lovasz local lemma applies, then runs Moser and Tardos's resampling algorithm from 30 seeds. Every output is checked to satisfy the formula; the numbers of resamplings are compared with the bound m/d and with naive rejection sampling. Seeded simulation.

experiments.title: Random colourings and Ramsey lower bounds
experiments.summary: Tabulates Erdos's first-moment bound and the deletion bound for R(k, k), k = 3..10, against 2^(k/2); simulates 4000 random colourings of K_6 to compare the chance of no monochromatic K_4 with the guarantee 1 - E; and verifies by exhaustive search that the Paley graph on 17 vertices gives R(4, 4) > 17. Exact bounds, exhaustive check, seeded simulation.

experiments.title: Galileo, d'Alembert and de Mere: dice questions settled by counting
experiments.summary: Lists every outcome of rolling two and three dice, tossing two coins and rolling one die four times, and counts favourable outcomes exactly with fractions: the triangular distribution of two-dice sums, Galileo's 25 versus 27 ways for sums 9 and 10, d'Alembert's 3/4, and de Mere's 671/1296. His 24-roll bet is too large to list and uses the complement rule. Exact under the assumption of fair, independent dice.

experiments.title: Relative frequency versus probability: simulated dice and coins
experiments.summary: Rolls two simulated dice up to 60,000 times (seeded) and compares the relative frequency of each sum with its exact probability; the largest error shrinks roughly like 1/sqrt(n). Also checks that after three tails in a row a simulated coin still lands heads about half the time, and that six rolls contain exactly one six only about 40% of the time (exactly (5/6)^5). Statistical evidence from one run.

experiments.title: Bayes' theorem with natural frequencies and base rates
experiments.summary: Builds the exact two-way table for a test with 95% sensitivity and 95% specificity on 100,000 people with a 1% base rate: only 19/118 (about 16%) of positives have the condition. Recomputes P(condition | positive) for base rates from 0.1% to 50%, updates after a second positive test, and shows the prosecutor's fallacy with a one-in-a-million DNA match in a city of two million. Exact arithmetic.

experiments.title: Conditional probability by simulation: dice, doors and cards
experiments.summary: Rolls two simulated dice 60,000 times (seeded) and estimates P(A), P(A | B) and P(A and B) for an independent pair, a dependent pair and a mutually exclusive pair, next to the exact values; plays 30,000 Monty Hall games (switching wins about 2/3 of the time) and draws two cards 60,000 times (P(second ace | first ace) = 3/51). Statistical evidence from one run, checked against exact probabilities.

experiments.title: Chebyshev, Hoeffding and the normal curve against exact coin tails
experiments.summary: Computes P(|S/n - 1/2| >= 0.05) exactly for n = 10 to 10,000 fair coin flips and compares it with Chebyshev's bound, Hoeffding's bound and the normal approximation. Chebyshev is always valid but very loose for coins; the true tail decays exponentially. A three-point distribution shows that Chebyshev's inequality is nevertheless sharp in general.

experiments.title: The central limit theorem at work: exact sums of dice and coins
experiments.summary: Convolves the distribution of a fair die and of a coin with P(heads) = 0.1 with itself n times (n up to 256), and measures the largest gap between the standardised distribution function and the normal one. The gap shrinks like 1/sqrt(n), within the Berry-Esseen bound, and is larger for the skewed coin. Floating-point computation of exact distributions; not a proof.

experiments.title: Fixed points of random permutations, all n! of them
experiments.summary: Enumerates every permutation of n = 1..7 objects and computes, as exact fractions, the mean and variance of the number of fixed points (1 and 1, as linearity of expectation and covariances predict) and the probability of a derangement, which approaches 1/e. The distribution for n = 7 is compared with Poisson(1). Finite cases only: the proofs cover every n.

experiments.title: Universal properties by brute force: finite sets and divisibility posets
experiments.summary: For small finite sets, counts the maps h with p1 o h = f and p2 o h = g for every pair (f, g) and three candidate products: only A x B gives exactly one. Then checks that products and coproducts in the divisors of 60 under divisibility are gcd and lcm, and finds pairs in {2, 3, 12, 18} with neither. Exhaustive for these finite examples only.

experiments.title: Binary by repeated division, and why 0.1 + 0.2 != 0.3
experiments.summary: Converts 45 to binary by repeated division by 2, compares the method with Python's bin() for every number below 1024, and checks that the binary strings without leading zeros of length at most 10 name each of 0..1023 exactly once. Then reveals the exact binary fraction stored for 0.1, explains why 0.1 + 0.2 == 0.3 is False, and redoes the sum with exact fractions. Exhaustive below 1024 only.

experiments.title: Testing conjectures with loops, and a bug that runs fine
experiments.summary: Checks 1 + ... + n = n(n + 1)/2 and 1 + 3 + ... + (2n - 1) = n^2 for n = 1..1000 with loops (evidence only; the lesson proves both). Tests Goldbach's 1752 conjecture that every odd composite number is a prime plus twice a square and finds the counterexamples 5777 and 5993 below 10000. Shows an off-by-one bug that runs without error but sums only to n - 1.

experiments.title: The cross-ratio under projective maps, exactly
experiments.summary: Works with homogeneous coordinates on the projective line in exact rational arithmetic: checks that 300 seeded random Moebius maps preserve the cross-ratio of random quadruples (including the point at infinity) while ratios of lengths change, lists the six values under the 24 orderings, and predicts a fence post's position in a perspective photo.

experiments.title: Finite projective planes: incidence, conics, Desargues, Pappus
experiments.summary: Builds PG(2, p) over the integers mod p for p = 2, 3, 5, 7, verifies by exhaustion that it has p^2 + p + 1 points and lines with p + 1 points on each line, that two points determine one line and two lines meet in one point, counts the p + 1 points of a conic, and tests Desargues' and Pappus' theorems on seeded random configurations in PG(2, 7).

experiments.title: Regions of a circle: a pattern that breaks
experiments.summary: Counts exactly, with rational arithmetic, the regions formed by all chords between n points on a circle (n = 1 to 8). The counts 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 suggest 2^(n-1), but n = 6 gives 31 (and 30 when three diagonals meet). The counts use Euler's formula, a theorem; the first five values alone proved nothing.

experiments.title: Euclid's numbers and induction formulas, checked
experiments.summary: Factors 2*3*5*...*p + 1 for the first nine primes (30031 = 59 * 509 is not prime, but every factor is a new prime), and checks Gauss's sum formula and the sum of odd numbers for every n up to 10000, plus a fake theorem that fails at every n. Finite checks support the induction proofs in the lesson; they do not replace them.

experiments.title: Cut-free proof search and the subformula property
experiments.summary: Searches for cut-free proofs in a one-sided propositional sequent calculus, checks the subformula property of every proof found, extracts a falsifying valuation when the search fails, and compares proof sizes for |- A*, A under two search orders (exponential versus linear). Exact for the formulas shown; it says nothing about first-order logic or about the cost of eliminating cuts.

experiments.title: Goodstein sequences and ordinals below epsilon_0
experiments.summary: Computes Goodstein sequences by hereditary base change, attaches to each term its ordinal below epsilon_0 (base replaced by omega, in Cantor normal form), and checks exactly that the ordinals strictly decrease along the computed terms. A finite check: termination for every n is Goodstein's theorem, which needs induction up to epsilon_0 and is unprovable in PA.

experiments.title: Truth tables: equivalence, connectives and normal forms
experiments.summary: Computes the truth tables of p -> q, its converse, inverse and contrapositive, checks De Morgan's laws and not(p -> q) = p and not q on every row, and builds a formula (disjunctive normal form, and a NAND-only version) for each of the 16 two-variable truth tables. Checking all rows is a complete verification for propositional formulas, provided the program itself is correct.

experiments.title: Right, acute or obtuse? Every triangle with sides up to 20
experiments.summary: Builds every triangle with whole-number sides up to 20 in coordinates, finds the exact x-coordinate (a^2 + b^2 - c^2) / (2a) of its top vertex, measures the angle opposite the longest side numerically, and checks that the angle is 90, under 90 or over 90 degrees exactly when a^2 + b^2 equals, exceeds or falls short of c^2. Exhaustive for these triangles.

experiments.title: Pythagorean triples up to 100
experiments.summary: Finds all 52 Pythagorean triples with hypotenuse at most 100 by brute force, of which 16 are primitive, and checks that Euclid's formula with m > n coprime and not both odd produces exactly those 16. Every triple is a multiple of a primitive one, and abc is a multiple of 60 in every case found. Exhaustive for c <= 100; the general facts need proofs.

experiments.title: Catastrophic cancellation in the quadratic formula
experiments.summary: Computes the small root of x^2 - Bx + 1 = 0 for B = 10^2 ... 10^8 with double-precision floats in two ways: the textbook formula, which loses accuracy to cancellation, and Vieta's product r1 r2 = c/a, which does not. Errors are measured against 60-digit decimal reference values.

experiments.title: How often does a quadratic have real roots?
experiments.summary: Classifies all 1,210 quadratics with integer coefficients from -5 to 5 by the sign of the discriminant and checks the quadratic formula exactly whenever the roots are rational; then estimates by simulation how often a quadratic with random coefficients in [-1, 1] has real roots, compared with the exact value (41 + 6 ln 2)/72.

experiments.title: For all and there exists, as all() and any()
experiments.summary: Evaluates quantified statements on finite sets with all() and any(), checks both negation rules for all 63 predicates on universes with at most five elements, shows that all() of nothing is True (vacuous truth), and compares 'for all x there is y' with 'there is y for all x'. Finite checks only: they illustrate the rules the lesson proves, and show how cutting N off at a finite size changes answers.

experiments.title: Set-builder notation in Python, and lists that miss numbers
experiments.summary: Writes set-builder descriptions as Python set comprehensions: two descriptions of the even numbers agree on 0..999, and small sets such as {x in Z : x*x < 10} are listed. Then, for sample finite lists of natural numbers, it finds a missing natural number (largest + 1) and a missing even number. Exact on the cases shown; the lesson's proofs cover every list.

experiments.title: Truncated ladder operators and the uncertainty relation
experiments.summary: Builds the N-level ladder matrices, computes [a, a^dagger] exactly (diag(1, ..., 1, 1 - N), trace 0: the canonical commutation relation cannot hold in finite dimensions), confirms that a^dagger a has eigenvalues 0, ..., N - 1, and checks the Robertson uncertainty inequality for number states and 200 seeded random states. A finite check of theorems proved in the lesson.

experiments.title: Harmonic oscillator levels from a finite-difference Hamiltonian
experiments.summary: Discretises H = -(1/2) d^2/dx^2 + x^2/2 on [-8, 8] by central differences and computes the lowest eigenvalues with numpy for three grid spacings: they approach n + 1/2 with second-order error. The ground-state uncertainty product sigma_x sigma_p comes out as 1/2. Floating-point evidence for a truncated, discretised operator; the exact spectrum is derived in the lesson with ladder operators.

experiments.title: Quiver roots: reflections, brute force and knitting
experiments.summary: For Dynkin quivers of types A, D and E it counts positive roots (Tits form 1) by reflections, by brute force, and by iterating the inverse Coxeter transformation on projectives (knitting the preprojective component). For the Kronecker quiver knitting never stops, and the indecomposables of dimension (1, 1) over F_p are counted: p + 1. Exact for these examples; Gabriel's theorem proves the pattern.

experiments.title: Cosets that multiply, and cosets that do not
experiments.summary: For every subgroup of S3, D4 and A4 it checks whether multiplying cosets by representatives gives an answer independent of the representatives, and whether the subgroup is normal; the two always agree. It lists quotient groups G/N with their element orders and gives explicit witnesses of failure for non-normal subgroups. Exhaustive for these groups only.

experiments.title: Finite fields as quotient rings F_p[x]/(f)
experiments.summary: Constructs F_p[x]/(f) for several small p and f, tests every element for an inverse, and confirms that the quotient is a field exactly when f is irreducible (F4, F8, F9, F16 succeed; F2[x]/(x^2+1) and F3[x]/(x^2+x+1) fail). Finds generators of the multiplicative groups and checks the Chinese remainder theorem for Z/12. Exhaustive for these cases only.

experiments.title: Percolation crossings and the Erdos-Renyi giant component
experiments.summary: Monte Carlo estimates of left-right crossing probabilities for bond percolation on self-dual (L+1) x L rectangles (L = 8, 24) for p from 0.35 to 0.65, which sharpen around Kesten's p_c = 1/2, and of the largest component of random graphs with n = 2000 vertices and average degree c, compared with the branching-process prediction beta = 1 - exp(-c beta). Statistical evidence from small samples, not proof.

experiments.title: Polya's theorem: return probabilities in dimensions 1, 2 and 3
experiments.summary: Checks by exhaustive enumeration that the number of closed walks of length 2n on Z^2 is C(2n, n)^2, then sums exact return probabilities of simple random walk on Z, Z^2 and Z^3: the expected number of returns grows like sqrt(N), like log(N)/pi, and converges to Watson's constant 1.5164 (return probability 0.3405). Partial sums are evidence; divergence and convergence are proved in the lesson.

experiments.title: Does a random walk come home? Statistical evidence
experiments.summary: Simulates 4000 seeded random walks on the integers, estimates the chance of returning to 0 within 2, 10, 100 and 1000 steps with 95% confidence intervals, and compares with the exact formula 1 - C(2m, m)/4^m. Agreement is statistical evidence, which can never be certain and cannot show that a return eventually happens with probability 1 (Polya's theorem).

experiments.title: Long division: why the decimals of a fraction repeat
experiments.summary: Runs long division with exact integers, tracking remainders to find the repeating block of a/b. Checks every fraction with denominator up to 200: the period never exceeds b - 1, terminating decimals are exactly those whose reduced denominator is built from 2s and 5s, and every expansion converts back to the original fraction. Finite evidence; the lesson's pigeonhole proof covers all fractions.

experiments.title: Rationals squeeze the square root of 2 but never hit it
experiments.summary: Searches every fraction with denominator up to 2000 for one whose square is exactly 2 (none exists), squeezes the square root of 2 between rational endpoints by repeated halving, and lists fractions p/q with p*p - 2*q*q = +-1 whose squares miss 2 by exactly 1/q**2. Exact arithmetic; finite evidence only - the proof is in the lesson.

experiments.title: Percentage changes multiply, they do not add
experiments.summary: Computes exact multipliers for successive percentage changes with fractions: up p% then down p% gives 1 - (p/100)^2; adding two percentages gives the right answer only when one of them is 0 (searched for all whole p, q from -99 to 100); a rise of p% is undone by a fall of 100p/(100 + p)%; five 10% rises give 61.051%, not 50%. Exact, finite checks of identities the lesson proves in general.

experiments.title: Proportional, linear or neither? Classifying tables exactly
experiments.summary: Classifies tables of (x, y) pairs as proportional (constant ratio y/x, through the origin), linear but not proportional (constant slope only) or not linear, using exact fractions; finds the constant of proportionality; and shows that adding two rows of a table gives a valid row only for proportional tables. Exact for the tables shown; a finite table can never prove what happens between its rows.

experiments.title: Mertens and Goldbach: the same kind of evidence, different fates
experiments.summary: Computes the Mertens function up to 10^6 with a Moebius sieve (max |M(n)|/sqrt(n) stays well below 1) and the number of Goldbach representations of every even n up to 2 x 10^5 by exact convolution (the minimum per decade grows). Both conjectures look equally well supported; Mertens's is false (Odlyzko and te Riele, 1985) and Goldbach's is open. Exhaustive up to the stated bounds only.

experiments.title: Checking every claim of Zagier's one-sentence proof
experiments.summary: Builds the set S = {x^2 + 4yz = n} and Zagier's involution, and checks for every prime p = 1 mod 4 below 3000 that the map is an involution of S with exactly one fixed point, that |S| is odd and that the swap gives p = a^2 + b^2. Running the same code on composites, squares and primes 3 mod 4 shows where each hypothesis of the theorem is used.

experiments.title: Pointwise versus uniform convergence: sup-distances
experiments.summary: Computes sup |f_n - f| for x^n on [0, 1) and on [0, 0.9], for the spikes 2n^2 x exp(-n^2 x^2) and for sin(nx)/n, using exact formulas and a grid cross-check. Shows convergence that is pointwise but not uniform, a sequence whose integrals do not converge to the integral of the limit, and uniform convergence that does not carry over to derivatives. Finite computations: illustrations, not proofs.

experiments.title: Weierstrass's function: difference quotients that run away
experiments.summary: Evaluates Weierstrass's function W(x) = sum (1/2)^k cos(13^k pi x) at x = 0 and x = 13^-m, summing the infinite tail exactly in closed form. The difference quotients at 0 grow like 6.5^m, while those of every smooth partial sum settle to 0. This examines a single point; nowhere-differentiability needs Weierstrass's proof for every x.

experiments.title: Repeating and non-repeating decimals
experiments.summary: Finds the exact pre-period and period of decimal expansions of fractions by tracking remainders in long division, then computes 40 correct digits of sqrt(2) and pi with integer arithmetic and shows where 22/7 and 355/113 part company with pi. Finitely many digits never prove irrationality: that needs a proof.

experiments.title: Squeezing the square root of 2 between fractions
experiments.summary: Iterates the map p -> (2p + 2)/(p + 2) in exact rational arithmetic from below and from above sqrt(2), showing that no rational is the largest with p^2 < 2 or the least with p^2 > 2. Then searches all q up to 100000 for p^2 = 2q^2 (none: evidence, not proof) and lists the near misses p^2 - 2q^2 = +-1.

experiments.title: Fibonacci numbers: recurrence, Binet, generating function, matrices
experiments.summary: Computes Fibonacci numbers exactly from the recurrence, from the generating function x/(1 - x - x^2) by power-series division, and by repeated squaring of the matrix [[1, 1], [1, 0]]; checks they agree and that Cassini's identity holds for n < 300; then finds the first n at which rounding Binet's formula in floating point gives a wrong integer.

experiments.title: Catalan numbers four ways, and their growth
experiments.summary: Counts balanced bracket strings by brute force for n <= 8, and checks the counts against Segner's recurrence, the formula binom(2n, n)/(n+1) and the coefficients of the generating function C(x) = 1 + x C(x)^2, found by fixed-point iteration on truncated power series. Then measures the ratio of C(n) to 4^n/(sqrt(pi) n^(3/2)) for n up to 1000.

experiments.title: Light bending and Mercury's perihelion from geodesics
experiments.summary: Integrates the Schwarzschild orbit equations u'' + u = 3Mu^2 (light) and u'' + u = M/L^2 + 3Mu^2 (planets) with RK4 and compares the deflection angle with 4M/b and the perihelion advance with 6 pi M/p for several impact parameters and orbits; the ratios tend to 1 as the field weakens. Then evaluates 1.75 arcseconds for starlight grazing the Sun and 43 arcseconds per century for Mercury. Floating-point evidence.

experiments.title: Schwarzschild: Ricci-flat, with finite curvature at r = 2M
experiments.summary: Computes with SymPy the Christoffel symbols, Riemann tensor, Ricci tensor and Kretschmann scalar of the Schwarzschild metric. The Ricci tensor simplifies to zero (a vacuum solution of Einstein's equations) and the Kretschmann scalar to 48 M^2/r^6, finite at r = 2M. Symbolic computation, relying on SymPy's simplification.

experiments.title: The twin paradox and velocity addition, exactly
experiments.summary: Computes with exact fractions the proper time of twins travelling at speeds with rational Lorentz factors (3/5, 4/5, 5/13, 12/13, 20/29), checks the reverse triangle inequality for 2000 seeded pairs of rational future timelike vectors in 1+3 dimensions by comparing exact squares, and verifies velocity addition identities exactly. Finite exact checks of theorems proved in the lesson.

experiments.title: Remainder families: residue classes that add up
experiments.summary: Splits the integers -12..12 into residue classes mod k, checks for k = 1 to 12 that the classes are disjoint and cover the range, and that the class of a sum or product depends only on the classes of the inputs, for every choice of representatives in that range. This is evidence for the general theorem, not a proof of it; a counterexample shows powers do not respect classes in the exponent.

experiments.title: Representable functors on finite sets and groups, by brute force
experiments.summary: Checks naturality of subsets versus characteristic functions for all maps between sets of size <= 3; counts all homomorphisms Z/n -> S3 and V4 -> S3 by brute force and matches them with solutions of the defining relations (the representing property of presentations); and applies the counting test |F(n)| = n^a or a^n to show that several functors on finite sets are not representable. Exhaustive in these finite cases only.

experiments.title: Character tables of S3, S4, D4 and Q8 from scratch
experiments.summary: Builds S3, S4, D4 and Q8 explicitly, finds their conjugacy classes, and extracts the irreducible characters from permutation characters on cosets of cyclic subgroups by repeatedly subtracting components and testing <chi, chi> = 1. It checks that the number of irreducibles equals the number of classes, that squared degrees sum to |G|, and that D4 and Q8 share a table though they are not isomorphic.

experiments.title: Maschke's theorem fails in characteristic p
experiments.summary: Lists all lines of F_p^2 for p = 2, 3, 5, 7 and finds those invariant under the shear (order p) and under the swap (order 2): the shear has a single invariant line, so Maschke fails exactly when p divides the group order. It also runs the averaging argument of Maschke's proof, which works for p odd and breaks for p = 2. Exhaustive and exact.

experiments.title: When checkers agree: independent versus correlated errors
experiments.summary: Computes exactly, in a toy Bayesian model, the probability that a proof is correct after k checkers accept it, for independent and for correlated checkers, shows the ceiling that correlated agreement never exceeds, and confirms the formula by a seeded simulation. It illustrates why agreement is no substitute for checking; real checkers do not follow this model.

experiments.title: Mersenne's list and other corrected claims, rechecked
experiments.summary: Runs the Lucas-Lehmer test for every prime p <= 257 and compares the Mersenne primes found with Mersenne's 1644 list, then rechecks Cole's factorisation of 2^67 - 1, Euler's factor 641 of 2^32 + 1 and Lander and Parkin's counterexample to Euler's sum-of-powers conjecture. Exact integer arithmetic; Lean rechecks the same facts in the lesson.

experiments.title: Riemann-Hurwitz and the monodromy of square roots
experiments.summary: Verifies the Riemann-Hurwitz formula for polynomial and rational maps of the Riemann sphere, measuring each ramification index by counting nearby preimages, computes the genus of hyperelliptic curves w^2 = f(z) and of Fermat curves from their branch data, and continues square roots numerically along loops to show the sign change round a branch point.

experiments.title: Complex tori, the modular group and the j-invariant
experiments.summary: Computes the j-invariant of the torus C/(Z + tau Z) from q-expansions of Eisenstein series, checks its invariance under tau -> tau + 1 and tau -> -1/tau, evaluates j(i) = 1728 and j(rho) = 0, and reduces points of the upper half-plane to the fundamental domain of SL(2, Z): tori form a one-complex-parameter family. Numerical evidence (truncated series).

experiments.title: Gaussian curvature from the metric, and Gauss-Bonnet
experiments.summary: Computes with SymPy the Christoffel symbols and Gaussian curvature of a surface from its metric coefficients alone (the Theorema Egregium in action): round sphere K = 1, upper half-plane and Poincare disc K = -1, torus of revolution K = cos v / (r (R + r cos v)). Then integrates K dA over the sphere and the torus: 4 pi and 0, that is 2 pi chi.

experiments.title: Geodesic spreading, conjugate points and Clairaut's relation
experiments.summary: Integrates geodesic equations by Runge-Kutta on the unit sphere and the hyperbolic half-plane and measures how fast two geodesics from one point separate: the ratio distance/angle follows sin t and sinh t, the Jacobi fields of curvature +1 and -1, with refocusing at t = pi on the sphere. Then checks Clairaut's conserved quantity along a geodesic on a torus.

experiments.title: Dilations change sizes, not shapes
experiments.summary: Applies dilations with k = 1/2, 2 and 3 to 200 seeded random triangles and checks with exact fractions that squared lengths and areas are multiplied by k^2 and that side directions are kept; angles are measured numerically and do not change, unlike under a horizontal-only stretch. Evidence for these triangles; the lesson proves the general facts.

experiments.title: Composing the eight grid symmetries
experiments.summary: Composes every pair of the eight rigid motions that fix the origin and map the square grid to itself (four rotations, four reflections), prints the composition table, and checks closure, undos, that two reflections always give a rotation (by twice the angle between the mirrors), how often order matters, and that all eight keep distances on a grid.

experiments.title: Unique factorisation in Z[i], and its failure in Z[sqrt(-5)]
experiments.summary: Uses the multiplicative norm x^2 - d y^2 to search exactly for irreducible factors in Z[i] and Z[sqrt(-5)], lists every factorisation of the integers 2 to 30 into irreducibles, and tests Euclidean division. In Z[i] factorisation is always unique; in Z[sqrt(-5)] it is not (6 = 2 * 3 = (1 + sqrt(-5))(1 - sqrt(-5))). Exact for the elements shown.

experiments.title: Units, zero divisors and ideals of Z/nZ
experiments.summary: Classifies every residue of Z/nZ as unit, zero divisor or zero, finds nilpotents, idempotents and all ideals by brute force, and checks for n up to 60 that units and zero divisors split the non-zero residues, that ideals match divisors of n, and that domain = field = prime. Exhaustive for these n; the general proofs are in the lesson.

experiments.title: Russell's argument as a finite search
experiments.summary: Checks every relation on sets of 1 to 4 elements (66 066 relations) and finds that no element ever has as its members exactly the elements that are not members of themselves; then builds the hereditarily finite sets up to V_4 and checks that the separated Russell set of each is not an element of it. Finite evidence for theorems the lesson proves in general.

experiments.title: Caesar shifts: encode, decode, and try every key
experiments.summary: Encodes and decodes messages with Caesar shifts (letter n goes to n + k mod 26), shows the wrap-around from Z to A, and breaks a coded message by trying all 26 shifts, scoring each against typical English letter frequencies. Trying every key is exhaustive; the score is a heuristic that a reader still checks by eye.

experiments.title: Breaking a substitution cipher by counting letters
experiments.summary: Encodes a paragraph with a seeded random substitution key (one of 26! keys), counts the letters of the coded text, and shows that the most common code letter stands for E. Matching letters by frequency rank alone decodes only part of the text, which is why code breakers also use word patterns. One paragraph, one key: an experiment, not a general law.

experiments.title: Geometric series: exact partial sums and gaps
experiments.summary: Computes partial sums of geometric series in exact rational arithmetic, checks the closed form a(1 - r^n)/(1 - r) for many n, and shows the gap to a/(1 - r) shrinking exactly (1/2^(n-1) for the halves, 1/10^n for 0.999...). For r = 1, -1 and 2 the partial sums do not settle. The limit itself is proved in the lesson, not here.

experiments.title: The harmonic series grows without bound, slowly
experiments.summary: Computes Oresme's blocks of the harmonic series exactly (each at least 1/2), finds the first n with 1 + 1/2 + ... + 1/n > t for t = 1..10 using 40-digit decimals (n = 12367 for t = 10), compares with ln n + 0.5772, and contrasts the sum of 1/n^2, which stays below 2. Finite sums show slow growth; divergence is proved in the lesson.

experiments.title: Checking set identities exhaustively
experiments.summary: Checks De Morgan's laws and both distributive laws on every pair or triple of subsets of a 4-element universe (a proof for that universe only, not for all sets), and finds the smallest counterexample to A - (B - C) = (A - B) - C, which does disprove that 'law' for sets in general.

experiments.title: Hidden squares on a dot grid, upright and tilted
experiments.summary: Finds every square whose corners are dots of an n x n dot grid (n = 2 to 6), upright or tilted, by exhaustive search with whole-number arithmetic, checks that a quarter turn of the grid maps squares to squares, and compares the counts with n^2(n^2 - 1)/12. This is exact for these grids only; the lesson explains why the formula always holds.

experiments.title: Sheaves on finite spaces: gluing, stalks and a first H^1
experiments.summary: On the four-point pseudocircle it tests the sheaf condition for every open set and every open cover: the constant presheaf fails, the locally constant functions pass. It computes stalks as sections over minimal neighbourhoods and the Cech H^1 of the locally constant sheaf Z/2, which is Z/2 as for the circle and 0 for a finite model of an interval. Exhaustive for these spaces only.

experiments.title: Negative times negative: grid, symbols and proof
experiments.summary: Checks (-a)(-b) = ab and (-a)b = -(ab) on a 21 x 21 grid of integers (evidence for those cases only), then lets SymPy confirm the identities symbolically, which relies on the ring rules SymPy has built in. Neither explains why the rule holds: the lesson's proof from the distributive law does.

experiments.title: Riemann sums and Simpson's rule: measured rates of convergence
experiments.summary: Approximates the integral of e^x over [0, 1] by left, midpoint, trapezoid and Simpson sums with 4 to 64 strips, prints the errors against e - 1 and the observed orders log2(E(n)/E(2n)), which come out close to 1, 2, 2 and 4 as the error theorems predict. Floating-point evidence for one smooth function, not a proof of the error bounds.

experiments.title: Taylor polynomials: Lagrange bound versus actual error
experiments.summary: Computes Maclaurin polynomials of exp and sin exactly with fractions, compares their actual errors (measured against the floating-point library) with the Lagrange remainder bound for several degrees, finds the degree that guarantees ten digits of e, and evaluates Cauchy's flat function, whose Taylor polynomials at 0 are zero. Numerical evidence for particular x and n; Taylor's theorem is what guarantees the bound.

experiments.title: Stokes's theorem and the periods of closed forms
experiments.summary: Checks Stokes's theorem for x^3 dy on the unit disc by quadrature (both sides approximate 3*pi/4), then computes periods of the closed form dtheta round circles, an ellipse and a double loop in the punctured plane, and of a combination of two angle forms in the twice-punctured plane. Numerical evidence, with the quadrature error reported.

experiments.title: Stereographic charts and the two transformation laws
experiments.summary: Computes with SymPy the transition map between the two stereographic charts of the 2-sphere, its Jacobian and determinant, checks that it is smooth and its own inverse away from the origin, and shows exactly at one point that vectors transform by J and covectors by the inverse transpose of J, so that the pairing is chart-independent while the wrong rule is not.

experiments.title: Thom's cobordism ring and Stiefel-Whitney numbers
experiments.summary: Counts partitions of n with no part of the form 2^k - 1 (Thom's dim N_n) and computes all Stiefel-Whitney numbers of products of real projective spaces over F_2, finding which bound and the rank of the span they generate. Products of projective spaces span N_n in even degrees up to 8 but never in odd degrees. Exact; Thom's and Pontryagin's theorems are cited.

experiments.title: Bernoulli numbers, the image of J and exotic spheres
experiments.summary: Computes Bernoulli numbers exactly and evaluates m(2k) = denominator of B_2k/4k, the order of the image of J in the stable stem pi_{4k-1}^s, and the Kervaire-Milnor order of bP_4k (28 exotic 7-spheres, 992, 8128). Compares m(2k) with the known stems pi_3^s, pi_7^s, pi_11^s, pi_15^s, which are quoted from the literature. Exact arithmetic; the theorems linking it to topology are cited.

experiments.title: Mapping cones and the non-functoriality of cones
experiments.summary: Builds mapping cones of chain maps between small complexes of rational vector spaces with exact fractions, checks d^2 = 0 and that f is a quasi-isomorphism iff Cone(f) is acyclic, and shows that the map induced on cones by a square depends on the chosen homotopy: the same square in the homotopy category induces multiplication by any scalar. Exact, on small examples only.

experiments.title: Least squares and correlation: Anscombe's quartet and confounding
experiments.summary: Computes exactly, with fractions, the means, variances, correlation and least-squares line of Anscombe's quartet: four data sets with the same summaries (r = 0.816, y = 3.00 + 0.500x) but very different shapes. Shows r = 0 for y = x^2 on a symmetric range, and simulates (seeded) a confounded correlation between ice-cream sales and sea rescues that vanishes once temperature is accounted for.

experiments.title: Sampling variability, margins of error and bias
experiments.summary: Draws 2,000 simple random samples of each size 25, 100, 400 and 1,600 from a town of 20,000 households with a known 38% rate (seeded). The standard deviation of the estimates matches the formula and halves when n quadruples; about 95% of 95% intervals contain the truth; a voluntary-response sample of 5,000 misses badly. Statistical evidence from one simulated run, compared with exact formulas.

experiments.title: How often do 95% confidence intervals really cover the truth?
experiments.summary: Computes the exact coverage probability of the Wald and Wilson 95% intervals for a binomial proportion for several n and p (the Wald interval can fall far below 95%), then simulates 4,000 normal samples of size 5 to compare the z-interval, the Student t-interval and the naive z-interval with the sample standard deviation, which undercovers.

experiments.title: The mean and the median as best centres
experiments.summary: Scans every candidate centre c from 0 to 50 in steps of 1/4 for the lesson's data, with exact fractions: the total squared distance is smallest at the grid point nearest the mean, the total distance is smallest exactly at the median, and the identity sum (x - c)^2 = sum (x - mean)^2 + n (mean - c)^2 holds at all 201 points. A finite scan; the lesson proves both facts for every c.

experiments.title: Mean, median and spread: what an outlier changes
experiments.summary: Computes mean, median, mode, range, quartiles and IQR exactly for a class's travel times, then makes the largest value ever more extreme: the mean and range move, the median and IQR do not. Also compares quartile conventions (they can disagree) and two bus routes with the same mean but different spreads. Exact calculations on small, illustrative data sets.

experiments.title: Multiple testing: false positives, Bonferroni and Benjamini-Hochberg
experiments.summary: Seeded simulation of studies that each run many z-tests. Null p-values come out uniform; with 20 true nulls at level 0.05 the chance of at least one false positive is about 0.64 (exactly 1 - 0.95^20), and Bonferroni brings it below 0.05. With 10 real effects among 50 tests, Benjamini-Hochberg finds more of them than Bonferroni while keeping the proportion of false discoveries low.

experiments.title: Normal equations and Anscombe's quartet: fit, then check residuals
experiments.summary: Solves the normal equations for a straight-line fit exactly with fractions and compares with numpy.linalg.lstsq; residuals sum to zero and are orthogonal to x. Then fits Anscombe's four data sets: identical slope, intercept, correlation and R^2 to two decimals, yet residual diagnostics reveal curvature, an outlier and a high-leverage point.

experiments.title: Geometric Brownian motion: Euler-Maruyama versus Ito's formula
experiments.summary: Simulates 1000 seeded paths of dS = mu S dt + sigma S dB by Euler-Maruyama with 2^2 to 2^8 steps and compares with the exact Ito solution on the same Brownian increments: the strong error decays like dt^(1/2). Sample mean and median of S_1 match e^mu and e^(mu - sigma^2/2); the naive chain-rule solution has the wrong mean. Statistical evidence for finitely many paths.

experiments.title: Ito versus Stratonovich sums along a Brownian path
experiments.summary: Samples one seeded Brownian path at 2^16 points and computes left-point (Ito) and trapezoidal (Stratonovich) sums of B dB, quadratic variation and total variation on dyadic partitions. The Ito sums approach (B_1^2 - 1)/2, the Stratonovich sums equal B_1^2/2, the quadratic variation approaches 1 and the total variation diverges. One path, finitely many partitions: illustration, not proof.

experiments.title: A Poisson process from exponential waiting times
experiments.summary: Simulates 20000 seeded runs of a rate-2 Poisson process built from exponential waiting times and compares the count in [0, 3] with the Poisson(6) law, estimates the correlation of counts on disjoint intervals and the memoryless property, and checks the convolution identity for Poisson probabilities in floating point. Statistical and numerical evidence; the theorems are proved in the lesson.

experiments.title: Hunting homomorphisms and isomorphisms by brute force
experiments.summary: Lists every map Z/m -> Z/n (m, n <= 6) and counts those preserving addition, finding gcd(m, n) of them; then tests all 24 bijections between four groups of order 4 and counts isomorphisms. Exhaustive for these small cases; the gcd formula in general, and the reason two groups are not isomorphic, come from proofs in the lesson.

experiments.title: Gluing polygons into surfaces: chi, orientability and genus
experiments.summary: Computes V, E, F, the Euler characteristic and orientability of surfaces given by edge words such as abAB (torus) and abab (projective plane), names them by the classification theorem, then glues a 2n-gon in all (2n-1)!! orientable ways for n <= 5 and counts the surfaces by genus, recovering the Catalan numbers for the spheres.

experiments.title: The Platonic solids: Euler's formula and Descartes's 4 pi
experiments.summary: Finds all (p, q) with (p - 2)(q - 2) < 4, then builds the five Platonic solids from coordinates, recovers edges (closest pairs) and faces (shortest cycles), checks V - E + F = 2 and adds up the angle defects, getting 4 pi each time: Euler's formula and Descartes's theorem, the discrete Gauss-Bonnet theorem; a picture-frame torus gives 0 = 2 pi chi.

experiments.title: Slides, turns and flips on squared paper
experiments.summary: Draws the letters F and H after a flip and after a half turn, to show that the two moves differ even when the pictures agree. Then checks on every point of a 21 x 21 grid that flipping twice undoes a flip, two crossing flips make a turn, two parallel flips make a slide, and moves keep distances. Exact, for that grid only.

experiments.title: Counting symmetries: every way to move the corners
experiments.summary: Tries every permutation of the corners of regular polygons with 3 to 7 sides and of six quadrilaterals, keeping those that preserve all corner-to-corner distances, and sorts them into turns and flips. Regular n-gons give n turns and n lines of symmetry; the rectangle gives 2 and 2. Exhaustive for these shapes only.

experiments.title: Symplectic integrators: energy drift and phase-space area
experiments.summary: Integrates the pendulum with explicit Euler, symplectic Euler, leapfrog and RK4 for 40,000 steps and reports the energy error, then computes exactly (with fractions) how much one step of each method scales phase-space area for the harmonic oscillator. Numerical runs illustrate, but do not prove, the long-time behaviour of the methods.

experiments.title: Shadows of a ball under symplectic and volume-preserving maps
experiments.summary: Samples random 4 x 4 symplectic matrices (products of elementary symplectic maps) and random volume-preserving matrices, and computes the area of the shadow of the unit ball on the symplectic plane (x1, y1) and on the Lagrangian plane (x1, x2). Symplectic shadows on (x1, y1) never drop below pi, as the theorem predicts; the others do. Sampling is evidence, not proof.

experiments.title: Guessing versus a system: missing outfits
experiments.summary: Simulates 2000 seeded guessers who name random outfits out of 12 and stop after 3, 5 or 10 guesses in a row with nothing new, and counts how often they found all 12. Also compares the average number of guesses needed to find all 12 with the exact value 12 x (1 + 1/2 + ... + 1/12). Statistical evidence for this setting only.

experiments.title: Organised lists: outfits, rows of children and handshakes
experiments.summary: Lists outfits branch by branch like a tree diagram, checks the product rule m x n for every m, n up to 6, lists every order of 3 and 4 children (6 and 24), and counts handshakes among n people both as ordered and unordered pairs. Exact for the sizes shown; the lesson explains why the patterns continue.

experiments.title: Invariants of the Euclidean, similarity, affine and projective groups
experiments.summary: Applies random Euclidean, similarity, affine and projective maps to random rational configurations in exact arithmetic and records which of seven quantities (distance, angle, length ratio, parallelism, ratio along a line, collinearity, cross-ratio) are preserved. Failures are genuine counterexamples; successes are evidence for the invariance theorems.

experiments.title: Products of reflections: the four types of plane isometry
experiments.summary: Composes random reflections of the plane in exact rational arithmetic, using the normal form z -> a z + b or a conj(z) + b, and classifies each product as identity, translation, rotation, reflection or glide reflection, checking fixed points. Even products are always direct, odd ones opposite, and three random mirrors almost always give a glide.

experiments.title: Mapping cones over F_p: exactness and non-unique fill-ins
experiments.summary: Builds random cochain complexes and chain maps over F_101, forms mapping cones, and checks d^2 = 0, the dimension formula equivalent to the long exact cohomology sequence, and 'f is a quasi-isomorphism iff its cone is acyclic', exactly, on 200 random examples (a quarter of them identity maps). Then counts the p fill-ins completing an identity square of triangles in D(F_p), by brute force.

experiments.title: Aryabhata's sine table, rebuilt
experiments.summary: Rebuilds R sin(3.75 n deg) for R = 3438 and n = 1..24 from sin 30 = 1/2 using only half-angle formulas and the recurrence sin((n+1)h) = 2 cos h sin(nh) - sin((n-1)h), and compares the result with the table of sine differences in the Aryabhatiya (499 CE) and with math.sin. Floating-point evidence about one historical table.

experiments.title: Trigonometric identities: numbers, triangles, symbols
experiments.summary: Evaluates sin^2 + cos^2 = 1, the addition and double-angle formulas and the false rule sin(a + b) = sin a + sin b at 1,000 random angle pairs, checks the laws of cosines and sines on 1,000 random triangles, and lets SymPy verify the identities symbolically. Floating-point and symbolic evidence; the proofs are in the lesson.

experiments.title: Type inference by unification: principal types as theorems
experiments.summary: Infers principal simple types of untyped λ-terms by unification (Hindley-Milner without let): the I, K, S, B, C and W combinators, Church numerals and addition, and terms that cannot be typed, such as λx. x x and Y, which fail the occurs check. Each principal type is checked to be a classical tautology, as Curry-Howard predicts. Exact computations for these terms only.

experiments.title: Inhabited types versus tautologies: proof search and truth tables
experiments.summary: Decides classical validity by truth tables and intuitionistic provability (= inhabitation of the corresponding type) by Dyckhoff's terminating calculus G4ip, for famous formulas such as Peirce's law, excluded middle and De Morgan's laws, checks Glivenko's theorem on them, and surveys all 102 implicational formulas with at most four atoms over p, q. Exact for these formulas, given correct procedures.

experiments.title: Words in L and R, evaluated in three monoids
experiments.summary: Evaluates every word in L and R of length at most 10 in the 2x2 integer matrices (L = [[1,0],[1,1]], R = [[1,1],[0,1]]), checks the homomorphism property, finds no two words with the same matrix, and decodes each matrix back to its word by Euclid-style subtraction. Compares with the non-injective homomorphisms to (N, +) and (Z, +). Exhaustive only up to the stated length.

experiments.title: Products of finite sets: existence and uniqueness
