experiments.summary: Checks exhaustively that maps X -> A x B correspond one-to-one to pairs of maps for small finite sets, then counts factorisations through three candidate products: an encoding of pairs as numbers passes, a set with a spare coordinate fails uniqueness, and the disjoint union fails existence and uniqueness. Exhaustive only for the sizes shown.

experiments.title: Equivalent expressions: tests, counterexamples and expansion
experiments.summary: Tests pairs of expressions such as 4 + 3(n - 1) and 3n + 1, or (a + b)^2 and a^2 + b^2, on blocks of integers and reports the first counterexample; shows a pair that passes four tests yet differs; counts exactly how often the false square rule happens to work on a grid; and lets SymPy expand each difference. Counterexamples refute; passing tests is only evidence; the symbolic expansion is a check of the identity itself, relying on SymPy's algebra.

experiments.title: Stiefel-Whitney classes of projective spaces
experiments.summary: Expands w(T RP^n) = (1 + a)^(n+1) in Z/2[a]/(a^(n+1)) for n = 1..16, lists the nonzero classes, and inverts it to find the dual classes. It recovers that RP^n can be parallelisable only if n + 1 is a power of 2 and that RP^(2^r) does not immerse in R^(2^(r+1) - 2). Exact, given the formula for w(T RP^n) and Whitney duality.

experiments.title: Cauchy-Schwarz and the triangle inequality, checked exactly
experiments.summary: Checks Lagrange's identity, the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality and the triangle inequality on all 15,625 pairs of integer vectors in 3D with coordinates from -2 to 2, using exact integers, and classifies the equality cases; then SymPy verifies Lagrange's identity symbolically. Exhaustive for this finite grid only; the lesson proves the general case.

experiments.title: Random vectors in high dimensions are nearly perpendicular
experiments.summary: Samples 300 pairs of random Gaussian vectors in dimensions 2, 3, 10, 100 and 1000 (seeded), computes their angles with the dot product, and compares the spread of cos(theta) with the exact value 1/sqrt(n) of its standard deviation. Statistical evidence from finite samples.

experiments.title: The column method for multiplication, step by step
experiments.summary: Implements the written column method digit by digit (with carries) and the area model, prints the working for 47 x 23, and checks the method against Python's multiplication for all 40,000 pairs below 200 (a complete check of those pairs) and 2,000 random large pairs (evidence only). A version that forgets to carry fails, showing that carrying is regrouping, not a trick.

experiments.title: Exactly one quotient and remainder
experiments.summary: Divides by repeated subtraction, lists all pairs (q, r) with a = q x b + r, and checks by exhaustive search that for every a <= 500 and 1 <= b <= 12 exactly one pair has 0 <= r < b, agreeing with divmod. This is a complete check of those 6,012 cases only; the lesson proves it for all numbers.

experiments.title: The Yoneda lemma by brute force in finite categories
experiments.summary: Enumerates every family of maps Hom(A, B) -> F(B) for functors on small finite categories (directed graphs, actions of a 4-element monoid, a group action) and keeps the natural ones: there are always exactly |F(A)|, matched bijectively by alpha -> alpha_A(id_A). Also finds the 6 permutations of S3 commuting with right multiplication (Cayley) and checks Yoneda for divisibility. Exhaustive in these finite cases only.

experiments.title: Hereditarily finite sets: V_n, numerals and pairs
experiments.summary: Builds the stages V_0..V_4 of the cumulative hierarchy as Python frozensets, the von Neumann numerals and Kuratowski pairs. Checks on all 256 ordered pairs from V_4 that Kuratowski pairs never collide while the encoding {a, {b}} does, that every non-empty set in V_4 has an element-minimal member, and that Ackermann's coding maps V_4 onto 0..15 with membership read off binary digits. Exhaustive only for V_4.
